entities.name: Modo Modo no Mi
entities.description:
The Modo Modo no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that grants the user the ability to generate pink energy which returns anyone and anything twelve years younger, which lets the user become a . It was eaten by Ain.

This fruit's main strength is that it allows the user to turn back the age of anything and anyone they touch, precisely twelve years. This can not only weaken or incapacitate an opponent, but also attack enemies in creative ways: for example, by transforming igneous rock back into its original state, this causes lava to erupt from the ground and injure an opponent, while reverting the ground back into a solid state after the foe is wedged into it to entomb them. By touching a person enough times with this ability, it can effectively kill the target by reverting them to before they were born, erasing them from existence.

The user does not actually have to touch the target, as one can charge and throw pink energy balls to the target in question. This fruit also allows the user to turn back their own age 12 years and revert to normal without falling unconscious.

Aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses, it seems to lose its effects when the ability user loses consciousness. Also, since the power is set at twelve years, the user cannot change the numerical value to whatever they please, and would require multiple attacks in order to revert the victim to the age they desire, and nothing in between.

The Mono Mono no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to create clones of people and objects, making them a . It was eaten by Pokke.

The fruit's abilities allow the user to create multiple clones of themselves or any other person or object they desire. The clones have the same abilities as their original counterparts, though their strength is not equal to the originals. The user also has command over the clones, even if the actions they are doing goes against their original personalities.

The standard Devil Fruit weaknesses apply to the fruit's user.

Pokke uses his powers to create clones of himself, other people and objects. He has created clones of the following:

The Mosa Mosa no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that grants the user the ability to accelerate the growth rate of plants and control them to their desire. It was eaten by Binz.

This fruit's main strength is that it allows the user to accelerate plant growth and then control such plants. The user can then control these plants to either ensnare their enemies or defend themselves.

One weakness is in order to use this power, the user must be in an environment where plant life exists, such as grass. Other than that, the user is affected by the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Binz uses his powers to make plants grow, in order to attack or capture his enemies or to defend himself from their attacks.

entities.name: Nemu Nemu no Mi
entities.description:
The Nemu Nemu no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that grants the user the ability to make anyone fall asleep. It was eaten by Noko in One Piece: Ocean's Dream!. In the anime, Noko demonstrated similar powers, but the fruit itself was never mentioned.

This fruit's main strength is that it allows the user to trap people inside a dream world while they are asleep. Inside the dream world, the user can steal people's memories to power up. The user can also manipulate the dream world using the stolen memories, as well as take control of someone in the dream world.

Noko mainly uses this power to put his opponents to sleep and absorb other peoples' dreams and to take control of people. However it is shown that if he is hit the memories will start spilling out of his body and back into those to whom they belonged. He also turns down the food Zoe offers him, saying he eats left over memories.

entities.name: Nepa Nepa no Mi
entities.description:
The Nepa Nepa no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to generate heat waves, making the user a . It was eaten by Wilder.

This fruit's abilities are rather strong, as it gives the user the ability to create heatwaves to overwhelm their opponents. The heatwaves can be powered up further if the user has certain tools, like Wilder's Basho Fan. The heatwaves can be so powerful that they can cause entire islands to begin to collapse.

The fruit's user is susceptible to standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Wilder used his abilities to launch heatwaves at the Straw Hat Pirates, pressuring them into being captured. He uses his Basho Fan to disperse and power up his heatwaves, and when he was cornered, he used them to try to destroy Promise Land.

The Nibi Nibi no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to take the appearance of the deceased, making them an . It was eaten by Kardia.

Whoever eats this fruit gains the power to control , flame-like spirits that, after touching a memento of a deceased person, can give the user their appearance and abilities. The will-o'-the-wisp can also be used for combat purposes.

The fruit's user is susceptible to standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Kardia used this ability to turn into Ace and Donquixote Rosinante to fool Luffy and Trafalgar Law respectively in order to defeat them.

entities.name: Noko Noko no Mi
entities.description:
The Noko Noko no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to create and control poisonous mushroom spores, turning them into a . It was eaten by Wapol's older brother, Musshuru, then later assimilated by Wapol himself.

This fruit is not to be confused with a Logia-class power, as the user cannot transform their body parts into poisonous spores.

The major strength of the fruit, as demonstrated by Musshuru, is that it allows the user to produce and control deadly spores from their body. The spores are so poisonous that anyone that gets caught in them would require the antidote immediately to cure themselves. While the spores by themselves are a danger, the user however can deploy the spores in any way he want, from small bursts or in a large cloud.

The major weakness of the fruit's powers is fire, which will eliminate the spores on contact. Either burning the spores themselves or setting the user himself on fire, can stop the spores before they can affect anyone. This Devil Fruit also requires the user to unleash a large amount of spores every 10 years to balance out its powers, an attribute not seen with other Devil Fruits by far. Other than that, the user is affected also by standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

entities.name: Nuke Nuke no Mi
entities.description:
The Nuke Nuke no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to phase through solid objects. It was eaten by Tanaka.

The main strength of this fruit's power is to allow the user to phase through solid objects, allowing for an easier and more unconventional way to get around, as well as avoiding attacks from non-organic weapons and projectiles. The user can also share their intangibility with whatever they touch, allowing people or objects to phase through solid matter along with him, or making the ground intangible to make people fall through the floor.

A weakness of this fruit is that the user cannot phase through living tissue, as seen when Tanaka could not escape from Robin's grasp or avoid Sanji's kicks. Other than that, the user is also affected by the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses. Due to this, the user apparently cannot phase through seawater.

As a security guard, Tanaka can use his fruit to easily travel to anywhere in Gran Tesoro where there may be a disturbance. Several rooms in Gran Tesoro do not have doors, allowing them to be accessible only by people whom Tanaka takes into the room. Tanaka sometimes uses his power against criminals by opening up the ground under them and sending them into a large cavern.

entities.name: Peke Peke no Mi
entities.description:
The Peke Peke no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform other people into clones of Peketan. It was eaten by Peketan.

It is unclear if the ability allows the user to transform people into themselves, or if it specifically transforms the user into Peketan.

The main strength of this Devil Fruit is that it allows the user to quickly transform enemies into allies, allowing him to overwhelm stronger opponents. People transformed into Peketan will work with the main body, working against former allies. People transformed into Peketan keep the clothes and weapons they had on them.

Aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses, the only other known weakness is an unknown time limit on the transformation, causing the affected people to transform into themselves. It is unclear how long the time limit is.

entities.name: Peto Peto no Mi
entities.description:
The Peto Peto no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-class Devil Fruit that allows the user to control any living creature by giving them a green, gel-like collar. It was eaten by Breed.

The power of the fruit allows Breed to control all living things by giving them collars. This collar first appears from his hand in the form of a green slime-like substance and is then either placed or thrown onto the victim's neck. The user can then control his victims' bodies against their will by issuing demands to them. The user can also bring out the full potential of its victim to use as his strength. The user can place a collar over oneself, and give orders to oneself to bring out his/her own full power and when doing so the collar begins to glow a bright red color. These orders can also cause the victims to levitate. Despite the usual Devil Fruit weaknesses, Breed's collars can work underwater without any apparent impairment, similarly to the keys Galdino creates that can open seastone handcuffs.

As the collars are projectiles, they can be dodged with ease by a sufficiently fast and alert opponent. Also, even though the user can control their victim's body, they cannot control their consciousness and senses, allowing them to come up with plans to escape the user's control. Another weakness is that the victim must be able to hear and comprehend the command for it to take effect, as seen when Breed had to repeat his order to Caesar that he "lie down" after Caesar failed to hear it the first time and when he lost control of Luffy and Law when they were wearing earplugs. If the victims exert enough willpower, they can resist the commands the user gives, as shown when Breed told his pets to get off of him while they were restraining him, but they refused to obey. If the user of the fruit is knocked unconscious, the collars that were already put on the victims will shatter and disappear. The fruit also lacks any direct offensive or defensive abilities. Aside from this, the user is still affected by the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses, although the power itself does not appear to be affected.

Breed uses it to control many animals like a kung-fu dugong, and even Chopper, by throwing collars at their necks which solidify and make them their "pets". He is also shown to be able to place collars onto humans, such as Luffy and Law as well as Caesar. According to Breed, he can do it with any living thing, turning it into his "pet" as well. Breed intends to use this ability in conjuncture with SMILEs to transform every human on the planet into animals and enslave them.

entities.name: Pocha Pocha no Mi
entities.description:
The Pocha Pocha no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to add excess fat on an opponent's body, making the user a . It was eaten by Neiro.

This fruit allows the user to control their own body fat and the body fat of their opponents. Its main strength lies in its ability to immobilize opponents and reduce their athletic ability by turning them obese. It even works on opponents who do not have flesh, like Brook. When the user reduces their own body fat, they can also harden and fortify their body, improving their defenses.

The main weakness is that the fat created by the fruit's abilities can be burned off easily with a high metabolism and rigorous physical activity. Otherwise, the standard Devil Fruit weakness apply.

Neiro uses his abilities to immobilize opponents and strengthen himself.

entities.name: Raki Raki no Mi
entities.description:
The Raki Raki no Mi is a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to steal another person's luck by touching them, making the user extremely lucky and the victim extremely unlucky. It was eaten by Baccarat.

By simply touching another person, the user will steal that person's luck to the point where they will become extremely unlucky, as multiple unfortunate occurrences will immediately happen to them. The touch appears completely normal, allowing the user to make their actions inconspicuous. Once the user has absorbed enough luck from other people, they become so lucky that they are almost invincible, as any attempt to hurt them will no doubt end up in failure and they can even use simple objects such as coins that will play out in their favor, like causing accidents that will hurt their foes.

One downside to this power is that its effect seems to be only temporary, as Luffy and Sanji stopped being affected by it after some time. Due to this, the luck that the user has stolen from other people can become depleted, either because enough time has passed for the absorbed luck to "return" to the user's victims, or because the user got lucky enough for all of their luck to get "spent". The user has no control on what the luck is spent on and it can accidentally be spent on something they did not mean to happen. If that happens, the user is unaware of it. Otherwise, the user is affected by the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Baccarat uses her fruit's abilities to bring down the luck of casino players, as their losses put them in debt and force them to work for Gild Tesoro.

entities.name: Riba Riba no Mi
entities.description:
The Riba Riba no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to reverse time around them, making the user a . It was eaten by Snitcher.

The Riba Riba no Mi grants the user the ability to reverse the movements of others or the flow of energy, including physical force. They have the ability to selectively enforce this reversal, applying only to specific targets, or to apply it over all eligible targets in a given area. The reversal of a person's movements additionally leaves them disoriented for a few seconds, and the reversal of energy allows the user to functionally reflect attacks based onto their user.

For the reversal ability to function, it must be manually activated by the user; it cannot be set to work automatically. This means that the user can only reflect attacks they are able to react to, and leaves them vulnerable if they are distracted. No other weaknesses are known outside the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Snitcher uses the Riba Riba no Mi to reverse the movements and energy of those around him, typically for combat or capture purposes. In combat, he frequently reverses the attacks of his opponents, leaving him nigh-untouchable in single combat. Additionally, he uses movement reversal to leave targets disoriented, allowing them to be easily captured, even by his weaker subordinates.

The Shuku Shuku no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to compress things, making the user a . It was eaten by Bolster.

The fruit's main strength that it allows the user to compress large objects into a more convenient size. This can be weaponized, for example, by compressing large bombs into a small size. The user can also compress intangible force or energy and then release it as a shock wave.

If the user receives damage, the compressed objects will return normal. Otherwise, the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses apply.

Bolster mainly uses this ability for combat.

The Ute Ute no Mi is a non-canon Paramecia-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to turn anything into a gun, making them a . It was eaten by Bad One Gracie.

The fruit's main strength is turning anything around the user into a gun or cannon. Any object such as a block of wood, a coffee mug, or a saber can be transformed into a firearm. Once awakened, it could turn surrounding areas or surfaces into firearms as well, including the sea, walls, and an entire island.

The main weakness of the fruit is that it permanently turns the user's hands into guns. Otherwise, the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses apply.

Gracie uses his abilities to produce guns and cannons and fire ammunition from them in bursts. He was also able to awaken the fruit's abilities.

entities.name: Batto Batto no Mi, Model: Vampire
entities.description:
The Batto Batto no Mi, Model: Vampire is a game-exclusive, Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that gives the user the ability to turn into a vampire. It was eaten by Patrick Redfield.

The Batto Batto no Mi, Model: Vampire resembles a small [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/tomato tomato]: a rounded purple fruit covered in the signature spiral patterns characteristic of Devil Fruits. Its top possesses a curled green stem resembling a tail, while the lower portion of the fruit gradually becomes dark red, giving the appearance of the fruit having been dipped in or filled with blood, in reference to the blood-drinking imagery traditionally associated with vampires. The fruit is small enough to be comfortably held within one hand.

The ability user can transform into a mythical vampire, developing numerous physical features traditionally associated with both vampires and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat bats]. In Patrick Redfield's case, his ears become long and pointed, his canine teeth extend into prominent fangs, his fingernails become elongated claws, and portions of his face and limbs become covered in purple fur. His body additionally develops pronounced bat-like characteristics, including large wing structures which can be used both for flight and as weapons in close combat.

Redfield is primarily shown fighting in a humanoid vampiric form that retains his general human proportions while adding the aforementioned animalistic characteristics. Sources associated with the game describe the fruit as permitting both a complete vampire transformation and a Human-Beast Form; however, the game itself does not clearly demonstrate a separate, conventional full-bodied Beast Form comparable to the completely animal forms normally displayed by Zoan users. As such, whether Redfield's demonstrated vampiric appearance is specifically his Human-Beast Form, his Beast Form, or whether this particular Mythical Zoan simply possesses an unusually humanoid transformation remains unclear.

entities.name: Tori Tori no Mi, Model: Nue
entities.description:
The Tori Tori no Mi, Model: Nue is a non-canon Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows its user to transform into a Nue hybrid and a full Nue at will. It was eaten by Toratsugu.

The fruit is biggest at the top and decreases in size as it goes down. It has a flat bottom. Like all devil fruits, it has a stem and is covered in spiral patterns.

The biggest known strength of the fruit is giving the user the ability to fly. As a nue, the user seems to be capable of fighting and causing destruction, as shown when Toratsugu attacked Lark and Kikuhime's wedding ceremony. The nue form is large enough to carry people on its back. No weaknesses are known aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Toratsugu uses his fruit in combat, as shown when he fought against Lark and later Luffy, and also uses its ability to fly in order to travel to places quickly and make escapes. When he lived alone as an outlaw, he seemed to be in his nue form most if not all of the time.

entities.name: Kumo Kumo no Mi, Model: Rosamygale Grauvogeli
entities.description:
The Kumo Kumo no Mi, Model: Rosamygale Grauvogeli is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a hybrid and full version of a Rosamygale grauvogeli, an ancient species of spider. It was eaten by Black Maria.

A user of this Zoan can become a Rosamygale grauvogeli—a heavy-bodied, stout-legged mygalomorph spider from prehistoric times—as well as a human-spider hybrid. Though an actual Rosamygale was quite small in size, the user's transformation will be proportionate to their natural body, which in Black Maria's case exaggerates her spider form's size to dwarf normal humans.

As the most notable of their spider abilities, the user can create sticky spider silk from their body, called |Hādo Gamu|literally meaning "My Thread"}} by Black Maria; while real spiders extrude silk from their abdomens, the user of this fruit can produce it from even their fingertips. The silk can be used to build webs and other structures meant for capturing and/or immobilizing targets, including sticky nets that can also be used as a shield. The webs are strong enough to easily keep physically powerful fighters tied up and, by Black Maria's own reckoning, anyone trapped in them will never be able to get loose. By making the webs into intricate arrays of traps, the user can make it so that no matter where an enemy steps, they will get captured.

With the webs being highly flammable, they can be used to instantly set the user's surroundings aflame by lighting them up, which Black Maria does by using the human face on her spider body, which curiously enough is capable of spitting fire from its mouth, though this may be due to additional abilities granted by Black Maria's tampering of her fruit's hybrid form via mutative drugs.

entities.name: Neko Neko no Mi, Model: Saber Tiger
entities.description:
The Neko Neko no Mi, Model: Saber Tiger is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a hybrid and full version of a saber-toothed tiger at will. It was eaten by Who's-Who.

A user of this fruit's power can turn into a "saber-toothed tiger" or Smilodon—a powerful, predatory big cat from prehistory that is characterized by its elongated, curved fangs on its upper jaw. The ability's current user Who's-Who, who is an already large man, grows to a very notable size in his full Beast Form, dwarfing his human-sized subordinates and a 3m-tall fish-man. The Human-Beast Form, likewise, is considerably large in terms of height and muscle bulk.

As with other Ancient Zoans, this fruit's transformation bestows greater strength and durability than regular Zoans'. The user gains a pair of long, sharp canine fangs usable for biting attacks, as well as retractable claws on their hands and feet, much like other feline Zoan powers. Those natural weapons are quite strong and can even overpower reinforced defenses. Amongst the Ancient Zoans, it possesses quite high agility despite the user's enlarged size.

Because Who's-Who gains a tail in this form, opponents may exploit this by stepping on it, preventing Who's Who from escaping their reach and forcing him into a precarious position for subsequent moves. Aside from that, no weaknesses of the fruit's power are known besides the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Allosaurus
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Allosaurus is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into an allosaurus hybrid and a full allosaurus at will. It was eaten by X Drake.

The major strength of this fruit is that it allows the user to transform into an allosaurus, a large and powerful theropod dinosaur from the prehistoric era. As a carnivorous Ancient Zoan, the fruit grants them features much better suited for close combat than basic Zoans, such as sharp teeth and claws. As is the case with every other Zoan ability, the user can also become a human-animal hybrid at will.

While in full Allosaurus form, Drake's own size increases, making him bigger than a Pacifista. He is also granted powerful sharp teeth and jaws that are strong enough to bite through a Pacifista's heavy armor, which is said to be stronger than steel. His tail is also a powerful weapon, capable of slamming people with great force. As with all Ancient Zoans, Drake's fruit grants him much greater durability than regular Zoan users.

In Human-Beast Allosaurus form, Drake becomes smaller than his Full Beast form but still relatively large and is capable of wielding his signature weapons for melee combat.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Brachiosaurus
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Brachiosaurus is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a brachiosaurus hybrid and a full brachiosaurus at will. It was eaten by Queen.

The major strength of this fruit is that it allows the user to turn into a brachiosaurus, a very large and heavy-bodied sauropod dinosaur from the prehistoric era, granting them an immense boost to their size and bulk. Their size is comparable to that of a giant, as a fully transformed Queen is shown to tower over Big Mom, who herself is extremely tall at over 8 meters.

Due to the signature long neck of the brachiosaurus, the user is able to reach targets that may be further away than they normally can by chomping down on them. The user's immense weight can be used as a weapon too, as very little will be able to withstand the crushing pressure of their massive, transformed body.

In addition, the brachiosaurus apparently has the natural yet unusual ability to separate the head, elongated neck, and tail from the rest of the body and have them act independently. The neck and tail form a snake-like component and can coil around opponents and crush them with immense pressure. However, the remaining torso and legs would be of little use without external modifications.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Pachycephalosaurus
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Pachycephalosaurus is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a hybrid and full version of a pachycephalosaurus at will. It was eaten by Ulti.

This fruit's power is to turn into a full and hybrid version of a pachycephalosaurus: a bipedal, herbivorous dinosaur distinguished by its super-thick, durable skull roof. The Human-Beast Form already grants a significant increase in body size, with Ulti going from an ordinary height to over three times as tall, and her full Beast Form is even bigger, at least as large as her brother's full spinosaurus form.

Much like other fruits of the Ryu Ryu no Mi series, this one grants its user a tremendous increase in physical strength. In spite of having proportionally smaller arms, Ulti is able to hold targets down in her full pachycephalosaurus form, shown when Monkey D. Luffy, despite being tremendously strong himself, found himself immobilized by Ulti's claws grabbing his shoulders and considered activating Gear 4 to escape her clutches. Beside strength, the user, in their less heavy hybrid form, becomes much faster, especially due to their strengthened dinosaur legs. Ulti is able to dart through the air at extreme speed by jumping, while proportionally increasing the impact force of her attacks in the process, and can casually dodge extremely fast-moving attacks, disappearing from sight.

With the transformation, the user's skull grows thicker and harder, which suits Ulti particularly given her fighting style that revolves around headbutts. While transformed, her large skull dome (more so her forehead in hybrid form) allows Ulti to potentially crush opponents' skulls completely with headbutts, like she already can in human form, strike large animals unconscious, as well as break through thick stone walls by charging into them headfirst.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Pteranodon
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Pteranodon is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a pteranodon hybrid and a full pteranodon at will. It was eaten by King.

A user of this fruit's power can turn into a pteranodon: a large, flight-capable, predatory reptile from prehistoric times. Once transformed, they become able to fly at tremendous speed, covering large distances rapidly, and enjoy a significant boost to their overall physical abilities, as typical for a carnivorous Ancient Zoan user. Additionally, the full Beast Form as displayed by King is notably large, several times bigger than an average-sized human (though it is worth noting that King is already much larger than normal people in his normal form).

Like other Ryu Ryu no Mi models, the pteranodon Zoan grants the user a tough, dragon-esque hide that significantly increases their durability to a level above regular Zoans. As for offense, the great (flying) speed, strength, and size conferred by the transformation allows the user to violently push back and cause notable damage to whatever they fly into headfirst, be it a person or massive structure (e.g., a large ship). The user's pteranodon beak is long, sturdy, and an effective pointed weapon, allowing King to affix himself to smaller targets and then divebomb into structures in order to tear them apart.

Moreover, the user is given the supposedly natural ability of using their pteranodon head like a slingshot of sorts: pulling their beak back into their face by pulling on their head crest, then releasing their grip to shoot out their head like a bullet, piercing whatever they aim at with incredible force. According to King, this conforms with how pteranodons used to hunt their prey in ancient times. Aside from their head and beak, the user's wings can make potent weapons as well given their sturdiness, able to generate cutting winds or clash against swords as if they were blades themselves.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Spinosaurus
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Spinosaurus is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a Spinosaurus hybrid and a full Spinosaurus at will. It was eaten by Page One.

This fruit bestows the power to turn into a Spinosaurus, a large and powerful, semiaquatic, carnivorous theropod from the Cenomanian stage of the late crataceous period (considered to be the longest megatheropod dinosaur ever), as well as a hybrid between a Spinosaurus and a human (or other) at will.

As with other dinosaur-based Zoan types, transforming into a Spinosaurus grants the user tremendous strength, particularly in their jaws, tail, arms, and claws (the latter in Human-Beast Form). In his Beast Form, Page One is able to smash and tear apart buildings and stone with ease using his maw and tail. In his Human-Beast hybrid form, he is strong enough to send a Raid Suit-donning Sanji flying and crashing through several buildings with a single swipe of his arm.

Being a dinosaur Zoan, this fruit bestows much greater durability than standard Zoan types do, allowing Page One to endure attacks from powerful fighters like Monkey D. Luffy or Sanji in combat. Against physically weaker opponents (such as Nami or Usopp), Page One can withstand multiple attacks in a row with little visible discomfort as well as recover from most strong attacks in a short amount of time. So far, only someone at the level of the Four Emperors has been able to deal significant damage to him, enough to knock him unconscious.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Triceratops
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Triceratops is an Ancient Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a hybrid and full version of a triceratops at will. It was eaten by Sasaki.

A user of this Zoan can become a triceratops—a large, heavy-bodied, herbivorous dinosaur from prehistory—and assume a hybrid form. In Sasaki's case, the full Beast Form is big enough to outsize a 13-meter-tall robot, and his hybrid form also stands taller than that very same robot.

Similar to other dinosaur Zoans, a user of this fruit is granted an enormous boost in physical strength. They can charge into and bash enemies with incredible force, their three sharp-pointed horns (especially their nasal one) serving as a dangerous pointed weapon to pierce opponents with. Given a triceratops' hardy skin, the user also enjoys a dramatic increase in durability, which especially applies to their frontal side that benefits from their thick skull, bony frill, and horns. This durability is such that the user may be unscathed by and able to outright ignore heavy, explosive artillery fire.

While the user's frontal defense is quite formidable, the entirety of their body is not so invulnerable, with their belly area being a particular weak spot. This was first seen when the "Franken" was successfully able to cut into and injure Sasaki's belly. Other than that, the user is affected by the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

entities.name: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Daibutsu
entities.description:
The Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Daibutsu is a Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows its user to transform into a Daibutsu (a giant gold Buddha) at will. It was eaten by Sengoku, the former fleet admiral of the Marines.

The main strength of this fruit is that it allows the user to transform into a giant, living, golden Buddha, gaining an extreme boost in strength to match the increased size. In this form, Sengoku's limbs grow out of proportion, giving him abnormally large arms and relatively tiny legs. His entire body takes on a solid gold hue (gray color in Gigant Battle); in addition to a full and hybrid transformation that are available to all Zoan Devil Fruit users, he can use palm thrusts to launch powerful shock waves.

This fruit has no apparent weaknesses, aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Sengoku has so far been seen using this fruit primarily for combat purposes, enhancing his punching power with his increased size, to the point of injuring Monkey D. Luffy despite his inflated and highly pressurized rubber body and destroying the scaffold they were on, even though his punch was buffered by Luffy's super-inflated belly and Galdino's harder-than-steel "Candle Wall".

entities.name: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Onyudo
entities.description:
The Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Onyudo is a Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows its user to transform into an onyudo, a large monk yokai, at will. It was eaten by Onimaru.

This fruit's ability is to transform into an onyudo: a mythical, human-like yokai that takes the form of a giant monk; Onimaru, in particular, stands at over four meters tall. This fruit being of the Hito Hito no Mi series, its transformation grants a nonhuman user human intelligence and the ability to speak the human language.

It appears that this transformation grants the user several bladed weapons, most prominently a naginata as well as a sword sheathed on their hip, that they can use in combat. When Onimaru transforms back into his normal form, the weapons as well as his monk clothing seem to disappear.

So far, no weakness of this Devil Fruit power is known beside the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

entities.name: Inu Inu no Mi, Model: Kyubi no Kitsune
entities.description:
The Inu Inu no Mi, Model: Kyubi no Kitsune is a Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to transform into a nine-tailed fox. It was eaten by Catarina Devon.

The main strength of this fruit is that it transforms the user into a mythological kitsune, complete with nine large fox tails. As such, they gain all the abilities of one, including the ability to disguise themselves as anyone they like, allowing them to impersonate them. The clothing of the target individual can also be imitated during the transformation.

The fruit has no known weaknesses aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Devon was seen using this ability to briefly impersonate the deceased Absalom and trick his comrade Gecko Moria. It is unknown if there are requirements to transform into a subject, in the same vein as the Mane Mane no Mi's ability requiring the user to touch a person's face in order to transform into them, though Devon notably expresses gratitude for being able to touch Jaygarcia Saturn's leg while in her Human Form.

entities.name: Risu Risu no Mi, Model: Ratatoskr
entities.description:
The Risu Risu no Mi, Model: Ratatoskr is a Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that grants the power to transform into a hybrid or full version of Ratatoskr, a legendary ice squirrel of ancient times. The fruit was "eaten" by the giant warhammer Ragnir.

The user is capable of producing ice and freezing mists that can flash-freeze targets. According to Loki, anyone frozen by Ragnir cannot thaw until Ragnir wills it; even an Omen blast from Nerona Imu was unable to break it. However, when Ragnir accidentally collided with the ice, it instantly started to thaw. By having the ice crystals collide with each other, the user can generate and amplify lightning, thus making it a good partner for Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Nidhöggr which produces lightning. The user is capable of unleashing ice attacks even when not transformed, making Ragnir doubly effective in its original hammer form. No weaknesses are currently known aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

As a hammer, the transmutation of the fruit's abilities has given Ragnir sentience, allowing it to use its tremendous power entirely of its own accord and select a worthy wielder. In conjunction with its current wielder Loki, Ragnir frequently generates either lightning or ice when Loki swings it to attack.

Elbaph legend holds that Ratatoskr was once the companion of the Warrior God many centuries ago, with the Warrior God also wielding Ragnir. When the Warrior God died, it is believed that the spirit of Ratatoskr inhabited Ragnir. The accuracy of this account is currently uncertain, but by gaining the powers of this fruit, Ragnir did receive Ratatoskr's goal of protecting the Warrior God's Devil Fruit, the Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Nidhöggr, which it did for centuries until being bested by Loki, who gained Ragnir as his weapon.

entities.name: Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Kirin
entities.description:
The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Kirin is a Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that grants the power to transform into a and half-qilin hybrid, which can put others to sleep and manifest their dreams into reality, making the user a . The fruit was eaten by Rimoshifu Killingham.

A user of this fruit's power can transform into a mythical qilin. Their qilin form comes with an elongated neck and a head that seem both draconic and giraffine in appearance, as well as an ungulate body. The user's skin becomes jet-black and is contrasted by wild, golden-yellow hair that looks flaming and cloud-like; this hair grows on their head, down the sides of their face (paired with matching eyebrows), down the back of their neck as a mane, and over their chest. The user gains a single straight, backwards, pale-brown horn on their head, two ungulate ears, dragon-like whiskers of pink color on each side of their snout, and a tail of the same fluffy, golden hair.

In their human-beast form, the user takes on a centaurian form, with their legs replaced by an ungulate's lower body akin to a horse's, with a light coat, while their upper body remains human (Killingham also displays sharp fangs in this form, though is they are part of the transformation is uncertain). Notably, Killingham has proven able to assume a form featuring a qilin head and tail, but with his body still humanoid from the neck down and able to stand upright; it is unclear if this is some partial transformation or alternate hybrid form.

In their human-beast form, the ability user becomes able to fly by creating flaming clouds beneath their hooves to tread on. On top of this and a physical power boost, the qilin transformation confers two special abilities: to make others fall asleep and to materialize their dreams into reality. To do the former, the user can emit ringed energy beams that put whomever they hit to sleep; these work even at long range, as seen when Killingham made several students of Elbaph's Walrus School pass out while being far enough away that his presence went unnoticed. While the ability user can forcibly re-awaken those they make fall asleep at will, it appears difficult for anyone else to wake them up. The ability user can also control the extent of sleep and, apart from full sleep, may induce a state resembling , wherein the victim is conscious yet their body immobilized.

entities.description:
The Uma Uma no Mi, Model: Pegasus is a Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruit that allows its user to transform into a Pegasus hybrid and a full Pegasus at will. It was eaten by Stronger.

This fruit allows the eater to transform into a Pegasus or Pegasus hybrid at will. This grants them the power of flight.

This fruit does not seem to have any specific weaknesses, aside from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Due to being a horse to begin with, Stronger does not appear to transform significantly apart from gaining wings. It is unknown whether this is his hybrid form or his full Pegasus form. He uses this power to carry Doc Q and other members of the Blackbeard Pirates while flying in the air.

entities.name: Jump Worlds
entities.description:
The Jump Worlds are a containing various Weekly Shonen Jump series' worlds, including One Piece. First appearing in the Jump Super Stars one-shot, the Jump Worlds would go on to be the primary setting of Jump Force.

In Jump Super Stars, the Jump World visited by Kobayakawa Sena is a large, rocky region. It contains a thick forest where he initially landed, as well as Dr. Mashirito's lab.

In Jump Super Stars, the only known permanent residents of the unnamed Jump World are Dr. Mashirito, Caramel Man #10, and Caramel Man #11. Monkey D. Luffy, Naruto Uzumaki, Goku, Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo, and Aya Toujou also temporarily take up residence in a cave in the Jump World.

Due to the Jump Worlds' nature as a multiverse, each universe contained within it also has its own resident characters.

entities.name: Uta World
entities.description:
The Uta World is an alternate dimension that is accessed through the Uta Uta no Mi. The user of the Uta Uta no Mi can forcefully transport anybody who hears their singing into the dimension.

The Uta World can only be entered by listening to the user of the Uta Uta no Mi singing. Doing so will cause the listener to fall asleep, with their consciousness transported to the Uta World. Once they enter, they will be given a physical form that is exactly the same as their original body, complete with the same clothing, weapons, skills and even Devil Fruit abilities. However, they will be unable to leave, being trapped until one of the following conditions is met:

If the user of the Uta Uta no Mi were to die while there are people inside the Uta World, they will become trapped forever, permanently unable to leave.

The Uta World also takes priority over other sub-dimensions, such as the Mirro-World and the Doa Doa no Mi's Air Door. While other sub-dimensions are still accessible from within the Uta World, they cannot be used to access the outside world, instead only connecting back to the Uta World.

entities.name: Impel Down
entities.description:
Impel Down, also known as the and the , is a government-controlled stronghold in Paradise together with Marineford and Enies Lobby. It is the World Government's maximum-security prison for the most dangerous criminals and pirates. It is located underwater in the middle of the Calm Belt and part of the Tarai Current.

Impel Down is the main setting of the Impel Down Arc, with the prison's staff acting as the main antagonist group in the same arc.

Impel Down is a large, submerged, tower-like structure whose foundation is at the very bottom of the seabed. Due to it being built within the Calm Belt, the entire structure is constantly surrounded by gigantic Sea Kings swimming below the water. Along with these beasts, the prison is guarded by a fleet of Marine battleships.

Within the dark confines of the prison are various cells and torture chambers that are used for the prisoners. The cells are all made from Seastone to keep those with Devil Fruit powers from escaping. The torture chambers are used for all sorts of brutal, unspeakable acts. Among these include continuous whipping, brutal beating to death, boiling cauldrons for burning and drowning, and spiked pits used for impaling.

entities.name: Ottankaina Kingdom
entities.description:
Rusukaina is an island in the Calm Belt that is to the northwest of Amazon Lily. Once home to the now fallen , it is a harsh island that has forty eight seasons a year which change almost weekly. It was here that Monkey D. Luffy spent two years honing his skills and mastering Haki under the tutelage of Silvers Rayleigh after the Summit War of Marineford.

There are several different species of dangerous animals on Rusukaina. Boa Hancock openly stated that the island is dangerous even by Kuja standards. The only safe area on the island is a tree which animals avoid. This tree is similar to Daft Green but does not emit poison.

According to Silvers Rayleigh, when Monkey D. Luffy arrived on the island, there were over five hundred beasts living there he would not be able to defeat unless he got stronger.

After the timeskip, Monkey D. Luffy successfully mastered Haki and completely conquered the island.

entities.name: Aoi Kingdom
entities.description:
The Aoi Kingdom was a nation somewhere in the Grand Line where Issho acted as the defensive military chief.

Nothing is known about the country's geography because it has yet to make an appearance.

The only known citizen of the Aoi Kingdom was Issho.

At some point in the last 44 years, the Aoi Kingdom was involved in a devastating war, during which time Issho served as the Captain of the Security Force. The war ended with the Aoi Kingdom's destruction and Issho's branding as a war criminal.

entities.name: Arlong Park
entities.description:
Arlong Park was the Arlong Pirates' base of operations. It was located on the Conomi Islands. This building, boasting several stories and their Jolly Roger at the top, was conspicuously placed at the coast to show that they had no fear of the law. The entire building was destroyed by Luffy's Gomu Gomu no Ono, smashing Arlong through five stories downwards.

Arlong Park was constructed along the coastline, east of Cocoyasi Village with an outer pool connected to the open sea—allowing for Momoo to go in and out—secured by a pair of steel gates. Nami's charting room was on the upper floors of the building; it was later destroyed by Luffy during his fight with Arlong. Overall, Arlong Park's design resembles Sabaody Park, a similarity Nami noticed. The building itself was modeled after the main building in Sabaody Park. This was due to the crew's childhood desire to become accepted into the human society, and mirrored the cruelty of Sabaody Archipelago's slave-trade.

The East Gate is the only entrance from the island; it was surrounded by paddy fields. It was destroyed by Monkey D. Luffy.

The Weapon Room, located on the first floor, held Zoro's Wado Ichimonji while he was imprisoned, until it was returned to him by Nami. The room also stored the Kiribachi, along with several katana.

entities.name: Baltigo
entities.description:
Baltigo, labeled as the , is an island located somewhere in the Grand Line. It was the Headquarters of the Revolutionary Army for years, and the island where Nico Robin spent two years honing her skills. The island's existence was long shrouded in mystery but finally became known to the whole world after its location was leaked. Baltigo was destroyed during an intense battle with the Blackbeard Pirates. Due to the island's destruction, the Revolutionary Army has relocated to Momoiro Island, which is now their new base of operations.

The landscape has tall rock pillars and the ground looks like it might be snow-covered. It is also very windy there. The island has some ancient ruins that served as the headquarters of the Revolutionary Army.

At least 14 years ago, Dragon made this island the base for the Revolutionary Army.

The island served as a hub of information for the Revolutionaries, and is a home to their leader Dragon and the other members.

entities.name: Flevance
entities.description:
Flevance, also known as the , was a country located in the North Blue, best known as the birthplace of Trafalgar Law. It was also notable for its abundant deposits of Amber Lead. It remains unclear whether Flevance was officially affiliated with the World Government; during the catastrophic outbreak linked to Amber Lead exposure, the royal family fled the country, abandoning their people with its aid.

A Hospital, with the stately appearance of a and fencing walls of wrought iron, stood as one of the many whitewashed buildings of the city, its color a result of Amber Lead. The hospital also served as an academy for promising young students, including Trafalgar Law, the son of the greatest doctor in the country. When Amber Lead Syndrome broke out, the hospital quickly succumbed to the crisis, crippled by a dire shortage of medical supplies and personnel as death tolls soared and outside aid never came. Law's parents were gunned down within its walls. The building ultimately burned down, claiming the life of his younger sister, Lami.

Flevance was often likened to a snowy kingdom from a fairy tale—its soil, trees, and grass all cloaked in a pristine white that lent the land an otherworldly beauty. So breathtaking was the sight that many visitors questioned whether the island was real or merely an illusion. Beneath its ethereal landscape, the source of its splendor was discovered: a rare and radiant ore, Amber Lead, that was determined to be the source of Flevance's marvelous white nature.

Following its discovery, Amber Lead became the cornerstone of Flevance's prosperity. The ore was refined into an array of luxury goods—utensils, paints, confections, cosmetics, even weapons—all prized for their brilliance and purity. Demand surged across the world, and with it, the town rose swiftly to wealth and renown.

entities.name: Haugen
entities.description:
The Sun World is one of the three regions of Elbaph. It is located atop the lower canopy of the Treasure Tree Adam, above the Underworld on the mainland and below the Heaven World on the upper canopy. Almost all of Elbaph's giant population resides in this world, including the royal family.

The Sun World is scattered across the Adam Tree's lower canopy, being too expansive to see all of it from any one place. Its villages and other landmarks have been built atop the tree's branches, resulting in the villages being difficult to travel between and thus quite isolated until the last century. Under the leadership of Harald, new branches were constructed that physically connected the villages, and the invention of the Svarr now allows for travel through the air. Notably, a gigantic longsword appears to pierce the Sun World, reaching all the way down to the Underworld.

The Sun World is high enough above the Underworld on the mainland below that an unobstructed fall will kill a normal giant. There exists an elevator, built from a set of boats tied to thick chains, that enables the easiest access from the Underworld to Sun World. There is also a rope bridge spanning between the Sun World and a castle atop one of the Underworld's highest mountain peaks. Those who sail in and out of Elbaph can directly access the Sun World by using a Painter stone to generate a rainbow to sail on.

The Sun World is dotted with forests of smaller trees and plant life growing from the Adam Tree. Hajrudin has implied that the region's animal life is nowhere near as big or threatening as those found in the Underworld. Since its settlements are built on a tree whose wood is flammable, the Sun World is at increased risk for destructive fires; an unlucky lightning strike may spell doom for entire villages. To mitigate these risks, the kingdom maintains a group of firefighters who operate out of a Svarr.

entities.name: International Philanthropy Federation
entities.description:
The International Philanthropy Federation, based at the temple of , is purported to be an international charity organization whose goal is to assist the poor. In reality, the organization is a sham, acting simply as a cover for its members to scam vulnerable people into thinking they are helping others.

The International Philanthropy Federation operates under the guise of being a religious group, dedicated to helping the needy. Fittingly, its members don religious uniforms and address their leader as , and their base of operations is referred to as a . They were apparently able to keep the scam going for quite some time, based on how much money the Rocks Pirates were able to steal. It appears to be recognized as a legitimate organization by the World Government and the Marines, as they were quick to send a large fleet to stop the invaders.

At least 42 years ago, the International Philanthropy Federation's temple, Foot Colony, was raided by the Rocks Pirates. Despite their attempts to stop them, the invaders were able to make off with large swathes of cash. Due to the destruction of Foot Colony, the organization's current status is unknown.

entities.name: Lulusia Kingdom
entities.description:
The Lulusia Kingdom was a historical World Government-affiliated kingdom located in Paradise. It was located south-west to Marine Base G-2, and close to Momoiro Island and Mary Geoise.

The country was ruled by King Seki, but following the events of the latest Levely, the citizens decided to revolt against him as part of the Eight-Nation Revolution and imprisoned him and his daughter, Princess Komane.

Following the Raid on Onigashima, the kingdom was completely destroyed without a trace by the World Government using an unknown weapon, fueled by the artificially created Mother Flame, and was subsequently erased from history.

Lulusia was stated to be relatively close to Momoiro Island. At the very least, Sabo took around six days of travel by ship to move through the two locations.

entities.name: Onigashima
entities.description:
Onigashima was a region of Wano Country. Originally a summit of , it became regarded as an island following the flooding of the country. It served as the official base of operations for the Beasts Pirates, including former Emperor Kaidou, the All-Stars, and the Numbers. The island was given its name upon being settled by the Beasts Pirates over 25 years ago.

As part of the New Onigashima Project, the island was displaced from its spot at sea by Kaidou using his dragon powers, with the intention of moving it to the Flower Capital. However, thanks to the efforts of the Ninja-Pirate-Mink-Samurai Alliance, the island instead landed safely near the capital. Sometime later, it was moved back to Wano's sea, where it sank down to the sea floor.

It is the primary location for the third act of the Wano Country Arc.

Before the raid on Onigashima and the subsequent New Onigashima Project and the sinking of the island, it was a mountainous island that was very difficult to access outside the front gate, which connected directly to the sea, allowing ships to sail in. The waters surrounding the island were apparently lined with whirlpools that made navigating around it nearly impossible unless one utilized specialized watercraft like a submarine. Thunderstorms were very frequent and even blizzards could happen, sometimes independent to the rest of the island.

entities.name: Prisoner Mine
entities.description:
The Prisoner Mine was a facility in the Udon region of Wano Country where rebels were worked and tortured until their wills broke, and they pledged allegiance to Kaidou. Additionally, it served as a weapons factory.

Following the defeat of the Beasts Pirates in the raid on Onigashima, the facility was shut down and subsequently destroyed by Admiral Ryokugyu when he arrived in Wano. Udon Castle is now being reconstructed over the prison's ruins.

The prison was predominantly run by its warden, Shinuchi Babanuki, and his vice wardens who were also Shinuchi of the Beasts Pirates. However, they were subservient to Queen, an All-Star and the ruler of Udon, who could take over proceedings in the Prisoner Mine as he saw fit.

Behind three gates, the Prisoner Mine is divided into six parts: the central Executive Tower and the five labor camps surrounding the Tower. This layout gives the Prisoner Mine an appearance similar to a blooming flower. It appears that each labor camp has a different purpose, with one being a rock quarry and another being an iron-works.

entities.name: Punk Hazard
entities.description:
Punk Hazard is a World Government owned island located in the New World and is the first island the Straw Hat Pirates disembark on after arriving in the New World due to a distress call they received.

A poisonous gas leak occurred on the island, causing the World Government to close off the island. During the two year timeskip, former Admiral Kuzan and current Fleet Admiral Sakazuki fought for the position of Fleet Admiral, causing each half of the island to be contaminated because of Kuzan's Hie Hie no Mi and Sakazuki's Magu Magu no Mi.

It is the main setting of the Punk Hazard Arc.

The island is surrounded by a sea of fire on one side and icebergs on the other. In the center, there is a hole where seawater flows into it, which separates both halves of the island and has sharks living within. This lake was originally a crater formed at the epicenter of Akainu and Aokiji's death match and then later filled with seawater, though the aftermath of the duel did leave behind patches of burning and frozen waters in the lake. This hole has fierce wind and currents running across it. As touched upon by Robin, the extreme temperature differences between the ice and magma lead to an equally extreme difference in air pressure, forming massive gale-force winds.

entities.short_description: Punk Hazard is a World Government owned island located in the New World and is the first island the Straw Hat Pirates disembark on after arriving in the New World due to a distress call they received.

entities.name: Skull Dome
entities.description:
The Skull Dome was the main landmark of Onigashima. The castle where the former Emperor Kaidou once lived was built inside of it.

The most notable landmark of Onigashima, the Skull Dome, is a large rock formation resembling a skull with horns that faces south-east. This mountain is easily visible from a great distance. During the battle atop the Skull Dome, Roronoa Zoro sliced off one of the skull's horns with Enma, and Kaidou melted the other with his Kaen Daiko form. Big Mom also caused further damage to the mountain while testing her new homie Hera, creating a three-level wide hole to the right side of the mountain's face.

Thanks to its enormous size, the dome's summit can act as a battlefield for numerous fighters, including even Kaidou in his gigantic dragon form. The top of the dome can be accessed from Kaidou's Castle through a huge set of doors, which allows even the Numbers to go and come as they please.

Most of Onigashima's buildings appear to be directly connected to the Skull Dome, making this landmark central to the Beasts Pirates' operations. The inside of the dome consists of various buildings lining the walls of the right and left side, with the castle being at the furthest wall.

entities.name: SMILE Factory
entities.description:
The SMILE Factory was a hidden facility situated near the secret underground trade port of Dressrosa. As the name of the location implies, the factory produced the artificial Devil Fruits known as SMILEs. It was eventually destroyed during the chaos of Dressrosa.

Before being destroyed, the factory was a circular building with a domed roof. Because Donquixote Doflamingo treasures this factory more than his own life, the outer walls were made of Seastone. The inside of the factory contained machines and large tanks for processing and storing SAD, and took the appearance of a large garden/greenhouse. There were trees and bushes growing the SMILE fruits, as well as a river with bridges for people to cross. At the top of the dome roof was a collection of luminescent sunflowers, known as Elegant Sunflower pointing downward towards the trees. Rotten fish were placed in an area with the sign "Meal" near it, indicating poor feeding standards for the dwarves. The sunflowers appear to have come from the Flower Field, as they share the same pattern. Somewhere was a so-called sickroom for Princess Mansherry, in order to motivate the dwarves to slave over SMILE production, but in truth it was a mere warehouse and Mansherry was not anywhere inside the factory.

The facility was situated underneath the Corrida Colosseum, and next to the Officer Tower, the hub of Dressrosa's underground trade port. After Pica reformed the landscape of Dressrosa, the factory was on top of a hill in plain sight until the dwarves destroyed it, which could be seen from afar by Trebol.

The unnamed bald worker is referred to as by the dwarves working in the factory. In the 8th popularity poll, the unnamed pig-nosed worker is referred to as . The term is a shortening of , meaning "petty underling" or "small fry".

entities.name: Third Research Institute
entities.description:
The Third Research Institute was a laboratory on Punk Hazard where Vegapunk performed experiments for the World Government. After Caesar Clown ruined the island with his gas weapon and the government's subsequent abandonment of the facility, Caesar made it his base of operations for the Underworld.

On the frozen side of the island the research institute is built into the base of a mountain and has a natural harbor in front that connects to the river. The building was originally the lab in which Vegapunk carried out his chemical weaponry experiments, but now it is used by Caesar as a hideout and for his immoral research. There are many different levels and rooms in the building, and each building is surrounded by balconies with chemical chimneys on the roofs. The building is marked PH-006 along with a gaping hole on the right side. Due to being on the cold side of the island, most of the facility is covered in snow and ice.

The structural layout of the research institute is made up of five large sections connected with each other via gates that can prevent hazardous materials from sweeping into the other sections. Each section is coded with the letters A, B, C, D and R.

The front entrance is well secured with shutters that can withstand explosives.

entities.name: Whole Cake Chateau
entities.description:
The Whole Cake Chateau was the four-layered massive castle of Big Mom, located at the center of Whole Cake Island. Following the detonation of the bomb inside the Tamatebako, extensive damage was caused to the Chateau's base, resulting in the collapse of most of the castle. Streusen transformed a large portion of the building into sponge cake in order to dampen the impact, thus causing the resultant product to cover Sweet City.

Whole Cake Chateau was the largest cake building found in Sweet City. The Chateau's exterior resembled a four layered cake, with the three top layers in different sizes, and each layer had a different style (horizontal, vertical, slash with horizontal base, and backslash), although internally it had a total of ten floors. The second layer had thin, red leafed trees on it edges, which gave the cake shape structure the resemblance of a birthday cake with lit candles. Another tree was occasionally seen on the top layer as well. The third layer had the kitchen's chimney on top of it across the fourth one. As the Chateau collapsed, it was transformed into a sponge cake, and the fourth layer was cut vertically.

The Chateau dwarfed essentially all the other buildings and landmarks of the island (actually being larger than Sweet City as a whole). It was situated roughly centrally on the island, being surrounded by Sweet City and Lake Aprico.

The is the name of the hallways in the Chateau. Luffy ran through one on the third floor, while he looked for Sanji. Another one on the second floor was partly destroyed when the chateau collapsed. Baum is German for "Tree", and considering the overall food theme, might come from Baumkuchen or Baumstriezel, which are types of Spit Cake, a kind of European cake made from rolled dough.

entities.name: 153rd Branch
entities.description:
The 153rd Branch is a Marine Base at Shells Town and the seat of the 153rd Marine Branch in East Blue.

{| align="center" border="1" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="0" style="font-size:95%; border-collapse:collapse;" width="100%" style="font-size:0.83em; background:#F0F8FF; color:#2A52BE; " ! align="center" scope="col" width="5%;"| ! align="center" scope="col"| Name ! align="center" scope="col"| Rank ! align="center" scope="col"| Status

After Morgan was promoted from the rank of Chief Petty Officer to Lieutenant Commander for reportedly capturing the infamous "Kuro", and later making his way up to the rank of Captain, he became corrupted by his newfound fame. He went on to tyrannize the entire 153rd Branch, along with the town under its jurisdiction, for three years—an abuse of power in which his son, Helmeppo, eagerly took part.

Their reign of terror came to an end when Luffy and Zoro defeated Morgan. Following his defeat, Morgan was dismissed from his position, and command of the base was handed over to Commander Ripper. Koby and Helmeppo remained part of the staff of the base until the transfer of the imprisoned Morgan to Vice Admiral Garp. During the transfer, Morgan managed to escape, after which Koby and Helmeppo came under Garp's command and began training under his tutelage.

entities.name: 16th Branch
entities.description:
The 16th Branch Base is a Marine Base and the seat of the 16th Marine Branch in East Blue. It is commanded by Captain Nezumi.

The 16th Branch is largely hidden in the manga, and its appearance is unclear, though it does have the dashed-line design characteristic of Marine bases. Atop the base sits a large model of a mouse's head; above the head there is a small tower with a surrounding balcony, itself topped with another set of mouse ears and an upwards tail that turns into a Marine flag.

In the anime, the base is depicted as a wide, short, blue dome, with smaller towers around it.

In the PlayStation game Set Sail Pirate Crew!, it is depicted as a green tower more similar to other bases, with a smaller tower alongside it that a cannon rests upon.

entities.name: 77th Branch
entities.description:
The Marine 77th Branch was a Marine unit active in the East Blue and led by Commodore Pudding Pudding.

The unit was sent to Arlong Park on a rescue mission for the survivors of Arlong's tyrannical reign. However, when its members arrived, Pudding Pudding saw the fish-man's base and gave the order to attack it. They fired a single shot, and provoked Arlong, who sent his crew out to attack the Marines. A squad consisting of Chew, Kuroobi, and Hatchan sank the ship along with its entire crew by creating an artificial maelstrom below it.

Though not shown directly, the 77th Branch was mentioned when Nami tricked Morgan, and again by Koby during Garp's pursuit of Luffy.

entities.name: Cocoyasi Village
entities.description:
Cocoyasi Village is the village on Conomi Islands where Nami, as well as her sister, Nojiko, grew up with Bell-mère. Situated in close proximity to Arlong Park, the village is home to the majority of key characters featured in the Arlong Park Arc.

When the Straw Hat Pirates arrived, it was dangerously close to being destroyed like Gosa Village. When Arlong was defeated, this village was the location of the ensuing celebration.

Cocoyasi Village is a fairly tropical place located in the seaside, with palm trees, mikan groves, and rice fields. It is located to the west of Gosa Village and east of the now destroyed Arlong Park. There is a simple wooden dock for ships as well.

Cocoyasi Village has a doctor clinic owned by Nako and at least one bookstore, from where Nami used to steal books.

entities.name: Frauce Kingdom
entities.description:
Ban Dedessinée is the queen of the in the East Blue and one of fifty monarchs who took part in the Levely.

Dedessinée is a striking and elegant woman. She has short, sleek, silver-blue hair, parted to the side and styled to frame her face under a pristine white headscarf. Her eyes are light blue, almond-shaped, and bordered by long, bold lashes and sharply defined, slender eyebrows. Her makeup is distinctive: she wears bold purple lipstick that complements the cool tones of her hair and eyes. Her complexion is fair, and her facial features are finely sculpted, with high cheekbones and a sharp jawline.

Dedessinée dresses in a sophisticated, high-collared crimson coat. Beneath her coat, the folds of her headscarf seem to resemble a regal white cravat.

When preparing for the Levely, she also wore a pair of stylish, gold-rimmed sunglasses with amber lenses.

entities.name: Gosa Village
entities.description:
The Gosa Village was a village near Cocoyasi Village in the region of the Conomi Islands.

Due to its inability to fully deliver the monthly tribute demanded by Arlong, all of Gosa Village's buildings were quite literally overturned by Momoo, the colossal sea cow under the command of the Arlong Pirates, as a show of force and punishment. The devastation occurred just two to three weeks prior to the arrival of Roronoa Zoro, Johnny, and Usopp. The only known resident of the village is a young boy, Chabo.

In the aftermath of the destruction, some of the survivors of Gosa Village sought aid from the Marines' 77th Branch, led by Commodore Pudding Pudding. However, the Marines' intervention failed to stop Arlong's reign. After the Arlong Pirates were defeated by the Straw Hat Pirates, Nami demanded that Nezumi's 16th Branch undertake the reconstruction of Gosa Village.

entities.name: Loguetown
entities.description:
Loguetown is a prominent city situated on the in the East Blue. Spanning nearly the entire island it occupies—save for a few steep hills—it serves as a vital port of call for the surrounding seas. Its strategic location, lying in close proximity to the Reverse Mountain and just beyond the visible reach of the Red Line, makes it an essential stop for almost all East Blue ships, especially pirate ships, seeking to resupply before venturing into the perilous waters of the Grand Line.

The town is famed as both the birthplace and the execution site of the former Pirate King, Gol D. Roger. This dual distinction earned it its poetic epithet: the .

It serves as the principal setting of the Loguetown Arc.

Loguetown lies just north of the Calm Belt and to the northeast of the entrance to the Reverse Mountain. As such, it serves as a crucial stopping point for East Blue pirates, who come to replenish their supplies before embarking on their journey into the Grand Line. Since Smoker assumed command as the captain of the local Marine base, numerous pirates were captured before even setting foot into the Grand Line's treacherous waters.

entities.name: Meshi
entities.description:
Meshi is a restaurant located in Syrup Village.

From the outside, Meshi appears to be an ordinary restaurant. It is just so in its interior, whose space is rather limited, making it a modest eatery where only a small number of guests can dine at any given time.

As soon as they reached Syrup Village, Luffy, Zoro, and Nami, led by Usopp, headed to Meshi in order to find something to eat. There, the Straw Hat Pirates got to know Usopp better, and the latter spoke to them about Kaya. Then, once Usopp left, the remaining members of the self-styled Usopp Pirates entered the restaurant and met the Straw Hats.

entities.name: Nagagutsu Kingdom
entities.description:
The Nagagutsu Kingdom is a World Government-affiliated nation in the East Blue that is ruled by King Furarri.

It is also the headquarters of the Nyornyo Nyarmani fashion brand.

Nothing is currently known about this island's geography as it has yet to make an appearance.

King Furrari and Prince Tritobu attended the Levely in Mary Geoise.

entities.name: Orange Town
entities.description:
Orange Town is a small, 42-year old town visited by the Straw Hat Pirates during the Orange Town Arc. Its mayor, Boodle, is not only the town's current leader but also one of its founding figures.

During its occupation by the Buggy Pirates, the town suffered significant damage, prompting most of the villagers to flee to safer parts of the island. However, once Luffy defeated Buggy, the townspeople returned to reclaim and rebuild their home. Luffy purposely left behind a bag of loot from Nami's stash worth 500,000 to help them rebuild their town.

Orange Town was built on a patch of wilderness near the sea by townsfolk who had lost their previous homes to a pirate raid. Built from the ground up as a fresh start, the town took on a colonial charm, with cobblestone streets and a quaint, seaside atmosphere.

The Pet Food Shop is a small establishment dedicated to selling food for pets, once run by Hocker. After his death, Chouchou, his loyal dog, took it upon himself to guard the shop in his master's memory. Tragically, the shop was burned down by Mohji and Richie during the Buggy Pirates’ assault on the town.

entities.name: Oykot Kingdom
entities.description:
The Oykot Kingdom is a country in the East Blue where Bell-mère first met Nami and Nojiko.

20 years ago, the country was ravaged by a pirate attack. In response, the Marines deployed Bell-mère and her unit to save the kingdom's citizens. After a hard struggle, Bell-mère, battered and disillusioned, lost hope of victory and was prepared to meet her end on the battlefield. But in that moment, Nojiko appeared, cradling an infant Nami in her arms. Bell-mère, moved by the sight, decided to take the two girls with her back to her hometown and chose to raise them as her own.

entities.name: Satsuruzo Kingdom
entities.description:
The Satsuruzo Kingdom is a nation somewhere in the East Blue.

Nothing is currently known about this country's geography because it has yet to make an appearance.

The only known citizen of the Satsuruzo Kingdom is Koby, prior to his kidnapping by the Alvida Pirates.

Two years before the start of the story, Koby set out to go fishing from the Satsuruzo Kingdom. However, he accidentally boarded the Miss Love Duck, and was forced to work as the Alvida Pirates' cabin boy.

entities.name: Shells Town
entities.description:
Shells Town is located in the of East Blue. The town is distinguished by its skyline of power plant-shaped towers, each bristling with cannons. It serves as the third setting in the Romance Dawn Arc.

Food Foo is a restaurant in Shells Town where Monkey D. Luffy and Koby discussed Roronoa Zoro and Morgan.

The 153rd Branch is a Marine base at Shells Town and the seat of the 153rd Marine Branch in East Blue. It is where Luffy and Zoro defeated Morgan.

It was the location of the Marine 153rd Branch, headed by Captain Morgan. Shells Town was being ruined by Morgan's actions until Monkey D. Luffy intervened. Since Morgan's "deposition" by Luffy, the Marine base was last heard to be under the temporary command of Ripper.

entities.name: Shimotsuki Village
entities.description:
Shimotsuki Village is a village in East Blue and Roronoa Zoro's homeland. It was founded by pirates, around 52 years ago.

The village was named after Shimotsuki Kouzaburou, a member of the Shimotsuki Family from Wano Country and one of the village's aforementioned founders.

The is a kenjutsu school, a school of Japanese swordsmanship. Its owner is Koushirou, who is a skilled swordsman and father of the deceased Kuina. It is the place where Zoro developed and trained in his Three Sword Style and, in the anime, it is the only dojo whose sign Zoro did not take down.

It is revealed that 12 years before the current storyline, the town was visited by Monkey D. Dragon and his revolutionaries, and that the dojo assisted them by providing supplies for the injured residents of the Gray Terminal.

entities.name: Syrup Village
entities.description:
Syrup Village is a settlement located on the Gecko Islands, as well as the birthplace of Usopp.

This is the main location of the Syrup Village Arc.

Syrup Village is a quiet community nestled amid rolling grasslands, dirt trails, hills, and forests. Its residents—including Usopp—live in modest homes, their simplicity contrasted by Kaya's grand and elegant mansion, which stands out among them on the top of a hill.

There are two slopes leading from the island's shoreline to the village, one located to the north and the other to the south. These passages are the only way to reach Syrup Village from the beach, as the rest of the coastline is marked by steep, impassable cliffs. Both passages are approximately three minutes away from each other by running.

entities.name: Tequila Wolf
entities.description:
Tequila Wolf is a massive stone bridge in the East Blue, which has been under construction for centuries. It first appeared when Nico Robin was sent there by Bartholomew Kuma during the events of Sabaody Archipelago. Both Robin and the residents of Tequila Wolf were later rescued from their enslavement by the Revolutionary Army.

Tequila Wolf is one of four monumental mega-structures that have been under construction using slave labor over the course of 700 years. The others include , , and .

The construction of the Tequila Wolf bridge has been an immense, ongoing project for the past 700 years, driven by the demands of the World Nobles. This colossal task is being carried out by slaves—criminals or individuals from countries that refuse to ally with the World Government. The building of the bridge has slowly progressed over the centuries, and civilization has had to progress alongside it, with earlier settlements crumbling over time and new ones founded as the bridge grows in length. Consequently, many ruins of former work camps lie scattered along the bridge, remnants of the grueling labor that has taken place over generations. The exact purpose of this seemingly insurmountable undertaking is still shrouded in mystery, though it was assumed that the goal is probably to connect various islands.

Four years before the current storyline, Bartholomew Kuma briefly travelled to Tequila Wolf in search of a cure for his daughter's Sapphire Scales.
