entities.name: Boin Archipelago
entities.description:
The Boin Archipelago is a series of flower-shaped islands in Paradise. Usopp was sent to one of these islands by Bartholomew Kuma during the events of Sabaody Archipelago Arc.

One of the islands is home to the swindling forest of . Also, it is known to have a forest made of food, called the . Within it live various gigantic bugs and vicious man-eating plants. This forest not only includes ordinary wild food such as plum trees and corn stalks, but also a river of already prepared ramen. In the anime, this forest resembles a food-based theme park more than anything else. Although it's mentioned there are thieves in Greenstone, the only known residents so far have been Heracles and Usopp, who was sent there by Bartholomew Kuma from the Sabaody Archipelago and spent two years in the Boin Archipelago honing his skills to eventually reunite with his crew and face the challenges of the New World. It is said that anyone who enters this island has no chance of leaving it again, though both Usopp and Heracles managed the feat.

The islands are actually giant carnivorous plants scientifically known as "Stomach Baron", that eat overweight animals that are in the Greenstone forest. A group of giant beetles guards the edges.

The 'islands' host a large variety of unique plant species known as Pop Greens. According to Usopp, the further one delves into the islands, the greater the variant of Pop Greens one can find. However, since the further you go in, the more difficult it is to escape, it is not wise to do so.

entities.short_description: The Boin Archipelago is a series of flower-shaped islands in Paradise. Usopp was sent to one of these islands by Bartholomew Kuma during the events of Sabaody Archipelago Arc.

entities.name: Forest Island
entities.description:
Amber Sleeping in the Giant Tree: Forest Island is an island in Paradise. It was created by the Great Tree for the ordeals that the Straw Hat Pirates chose to participate in. It was later reformed into Desert Island.

Forest Island was the first island the Straw Hat Pirates visited in One Piece Unlimited Cruise 1: The Treasure Beneath The Waves.

Forest Island is an isle with a rocky foundation, yet covered in rich earth and lush forests with trees, many of which are the size of buildings. Small lakes and waterfalls can be found across the island as well. In addition, massive lumps of crystalized orange amber at the size of native bedrocks can be found further inside the island. The landmark of the island is a colossal naked tree at the top of the island that is covered in crystalized amber.

The island has a few sandy beach areas at the foot of the cliffs near the beach with grass, palm trees and medicinal pants, although they are not necessarily wide. The main beach has terraced rocks to the west leading up to paths that wind throughout the southwestern sector, reaching areas such as cliffs and narrow passageways. Beyond rocks barring paths there are also an isolated beach and a cave in the bedrock. To the east of the main beach on the other hand are more climbable cliffs and a small beach with an ankle-deep seabed stretching out in front of it.

entities.short_description: Amber Sleeping in the Giant Tree: Forest Island is an island in Paradise. It was created by the Great Tree for the ordeals that the Straw Hat Pirates chose to participate in. It was later reformed into Desert Island.

entities.name: Green Bit
entities.description:
Green Bit is a seemingly uninhabited island in the New World located immediately north of Dressrosa. Law first mentioned the island when he was speaking to Smoker on Punk Hazard. Its underground is home to the Tontatta Kingdom.

Green Bit is connected to Dressrosa by an iron bridge and a secret underground passage. The presence of the Fighting Fish has forced the bridge to be closed for 200 years.

Befitting its name, Green Bit is a very green place, with a large forest and huge plants. Some animals, namely birds, foxes, and boars have been seen on the Island. Underneath the forest, there is a village which is formed by plants.

As a result of a meteor summoned by Issho, a large crater was formed on one side of Green Bit's shore.

entities.name: Jungle Zone
entities.description:
A Dense Forest Deep in Mystery: The Jungle Zone is the densely forested area of the unnamed island Popora inhabits. It is the second area the Straw Hat Pirates explore in One Piece: Unlimited Adventure.

The Jungle Zone is a wooded region of the game's unnamed island with thick vegetation and rich, porous soil. It is swamp-like in places, with ankle deep ponds scattered throughout. The plants have far more variety than in other regions, including different kinds of trees, large leafy plants, and Venus flytraps large enough to hurt a human. The region also has significantly taller trees than other parts of the island, some with roots large enough to walk on.

A large shipwreck can be found deep in the Jungle Zone, partially buried in a swamp and submerged in ankle-deep standing water.

The Jungle Zone connects to the Plain Zone, Seaside Zone, and Cave Zone.

entities.name: Little Garden
entities.description:
Little Garden is an island in Paradise. Due to the climate, dinosaurs are still alive there. This is the second island on the Grand Line that the Straw Hat Pirates visit and the setting of the Little Garden Arc.

Little Garden is a Prehistoric Island and as such is still in the age of the Dinosaurs. Not much is known about Little Garden, other than it seems to develop very slowly. Due to the extreme climate and dangers of the dinosaurs and the duels between Dorry and Brogy, no human has been able to stay there the entire year for the Log Pose to reset without dying.

In the anime, Dorry stated that one human left Little Garden before his log reset, but they didn't know if he survived.

The climate of the island creates a perfect habitat for dinosaurs. Because the Grand Line can have so many climates, Little Garden's climate is one of dense jungle. This has led it to be behind the average island in the Grand Line by millions of years. The climate is unbearable for many humans that plan to stay long, as well as providing ideal conditions for fatal illnesses to survive, some thought previously extinct.

entities.short_description: Little Garden is an island in Paradise. Due to the climate, dinosaurs are still alive there. This is the second island on the Grand Line that the Straw Hat Pirates visit and the setting of the Little Garden Arc.

entities.name: Midway Forest
entities.description:
Midway Forest is a forested area located between Mt. Colubo and the Gray Terminal. It is known for being a dangerous place to any human.

Portgas D. Ace and Sabo used this place as a sort of hideout in their youth, hiding the loot they obtained from stealing within a hidden storage in a large tree. A young Luffy was able to locate them and their treasure stash after following Ace through Mt. Colubo.

After defeating Bluejam in the burning Gray Terminal, Ace and Curly Dadan took refuge next to a river in the forest in order to avoid the spreading fire.

entities.name: Rusukaina
entities.description:
Rusukaina is an island in the Calm Belt that is to the northwest of Amazon Lily. Once home to the now fallen , it is a harsh island that has forty eight seasons a year which change almost weekly. It was here that Monkey D. Luffy spent two years honing his skills and mastering Haki under the tutelage of Silvers Rayleigh after the Summit War of Marineford.

There are several different species of dangerous animals on Rusukaina. Boa Hancock openly stated that the island is dangerous even by Kuja standards. The only safe area on the island is a tree which animals avoid. This tree is similar to Daft Green but does not emit poison.

According to Silvers Rayleigh, when Monkey D. Luffy arrived on the island, there were over five hundred beasts living there he would not be able to defeat unless he got stronger.

After the timeskip, Monkey D. Luffy successfully mastered Haki and completely conquered the island.

entities.name: Seducing Woods
entities.description:
Whole Cake Island is a New World island under the control of Big Mom, formerly one of the Four Emperors. It is her crew's base of operations and the central island in Big Mom's 35-island archipelago known as Totto Land.

In addition to other minor islands in the Totto Land archipelago, Whole Cake Island is the primary setting of the Whole Cake Island Arc.

The island is quite large, and until about 62 years ago, it was a regular island with several round hills. It was renamed to "Whole Cake Island" due to Charlotte Linlin and Streusen working to fulfill the former's dream, which was inherited from Carmel, and its new resemblance to a gathering of frosted cakes are due to the enormous cake buildings constructed there. Due to the buildings' enormous size, visitors tend to be awed at the first sight of the island. Atop the largest central building, the Whole Cake Chateau, there are massive poles shaped like candles, making it look like a birthday cake (being even depicted as lit, although it is unknown if their "flames" are real and the anime implies that they are trees). Most buildings appear to be covered in what looks like icing. The interiors of buildings in general look as if they are partly made of icing.

At least the island's southwestern coast is covered in a kind of hardened whipped cream, namely meringue.

entities.short_description: Whole Cake Island is a New World island under the control of Big Mom, formerly one of the Four Emperors. It is her crew's base of operations and the central island in Big Mom's 35-island archipelago known as Totto Land.

entities.name: Upper Yard
entities.description:
Upper Yard is an island in Skypiea that is solid land, unlike other Sky Islands, which are made up of clouds. It was the easternmost part of Jaya in the past until it was pushed up by the Knock Up Stream. Most of the Skypiea Arc took place here.

Most of it is covered by forest. The trees and animals on Upper Yard have grown to huge sizes due to the decrease in the atmosphere.

A Milky Road leads to Upper Yard from Angel Island.

Entrance of Ordeals is a gate in front of which people must decide on an ordeal of their choosing by passing through its respective gate. From left to right, the Ordeals that each gate leads to are: Swamp, Iron, String, and Balls. Above the entrance is the sculpture of the head of an idol. The only known area is the Lost Forest for the Ordeal of Balls.

entities.name: Bourgeois Kingdom
entities.description:
The Bourgeois Kingdom is a kingdom located somewhere in the Grand Line from which Cavendish hails.

Little has been seen of the kingdom so far, but there exists a large castle where the royal family resides. Directly in front of the castle is a stone path that weaves through a field of flowers.

Cavendish was born as the prince of the Bourgeois Kingdom, and even when he was a child he was admired by women. As Cavendish grew older, he got so popular that the women of the kingdom refused to get married, and he was eventually run out of the kingdom for being too popular, left with 74 underlings and 500,000,000.

entities.name: Mt. Kintoki
entities.description:
Mt. Kintoki is a mountain on an island somewhere in the Grand Line. It is Sentomaru's place of origin.

Little of Mt. Kintoki has been shown, but it appears to be covered in a large forest. A village is located very close to Mt. Kintoki, enough so that they are sometimes plagued by animals leaving the forest.

The only known citizen of Mt. Kintoki was Sentomaru, when he was a child.

As a young child, Sentomaru was banished by the village near Mt. Kintoki, and took up residence on the mountain. Using his sumo abilities, he began living on the mountain, eventually becoming the de facto master of the mountain.

entities.name: Standing Kingdom
entities.description:
The Standing Kingdom is Orlumbus' home nation.

Little has been seen of the kingdom so far, but there exists a castle where the king resides. The kingdom’s port was later shown during Orlumbus’ departure.

At some point after leaving Dressrosa, Orlumbus returned to this kingdom in order to resign from his post as an adventurer. The king, however, was furious at his resignation. Soon after Orlumbus set sail with his fleet in tow, the king ordered the kingdom’s army to fire on them as they left.

entities.name: Vodka Kingdom
entities.description:
The Vodka Kingdom is a World Government affiliated kingdom located in the Grand Line.

Nothing is known about the current state of Vodka, but around 40–50 years ago, the kingdom was very poor and worn down. In order to pay the Heavenly Tribute, Vodka was forced to wage wars against other countries and loot them, which it managed to accomplish thanks to the strength of its most powerful military asset, the young soldier Kaidou.

46 years ago, the kingdom attempted to gain the right to attend the Levely in exchange for Kaidou's forceful drafting into the Marines, but it is unknown whether they ever did due to Kaidou's subsequent escape.

The buildings in the Vodka Kingdom mainly consist of worn-down fortresses made of stone and bricks.

entities.name: Branch Route 1
entities.description:
The Sun World is one of the three regions of Elbaph. It is located atop the lower canopy of the Treasure Tree Adam, above the Underworld on the mainland and below the Heaven World on the upper canopy. Almost all of Elbaph's giant population resides in this world, including the royal family.

The Sun World is scattered across the Adam Tree's lower canopy, being too expansive to see all of it from any one place. Its villages and other landmarks have been built atop the tree's branches, resulting in the villages being difficult to travel between and thus quite isolated until the last century. Under the leadership of Harald, new branches were constructed that physically connected the villages, and the invention of the Svarr now allows for travel through the air. Notably, a gigantic longsword appears to pierce the Sun World, reaching all the way down to the Underworld.

The Sun World is high enough above the Underworld on the mainland below that an unobstructed fall will kill a normal giant. There exists an elevator, built from a set of boats tied to thick chains, that enables the easiest access from the Underworld to Sun World. There is also a rope bridge spanning between the Sun World and a castle atop one of the Underworld's highest mountain peaks. Those who sail in and out of Elbaph can directly access the Sun World by using a Painter stone to generate a rainbow to sail on.

The Sun World is dotted with forests of smaller trees and plant life growing from the Adam Tree. Hajrudin has implied that the region's animal life is nowhere near as big or threatening as those found in the Underworld. Since its settlements are built on a tree whose wood is flammable, the Sun World is at increased risk for destructive fires; an unlucky lightning strike may spell doom for entire villages. To mitigate these risks, the kingdom maintains a group of firefighters who operate out of a Svarr.

entities.name: Bridge of Hesitation
entities.description:
Enies Lobby was a World Government establishment located on a Paradise island where night never fell. It, along with Impel Down and Marineford, comprised the three major Government strongholds triangulating the Tarai Current via the Gates of Justice.

Reputed worldwide as the , Enies Lobby hosted both CP9 headquarters and the (mostly ceremonial) courthouse for processing Impel Down sentences. These were attended by a mixed garrison of Cipher Pol agents, Marines, and special personnel, totaling some 10,000 troops in all.

After a combined attack from Straw Hat Pirates, the Galley-La Company and the Franky Family—which inadvertently triggered a full-scale Buster Call—the island was completely annihilated, and left in ruins. It is unknown if anything has been rebuilt since.

It was the main setting of the Enies Lobby Arc.

entities.name: Flower Hill
entities.description:
The flower fields are a lovely field that are full of sunflowers with one big tree that is in the middle of the field.

Hidden beneath the flower field are the secret headquarters of the Riku Royal Army.

This is also the place where Rebecca's mother, Scarlett, is buried.

10 years ago, Rebecca's mother, Scarlett, met her end when she tried to get food for her daughter. While Rebecca was waiting alone in the red flower field, Thunder Soldier returned to her with Scarlett's body. Afterwards, they gave Scarlett a burial.

entities.name: Gates of Justice
entities.description:
The Gates of Justice are three massive structures that are each located at the World Government's three primary strongholds in the Paradise half of the Grand Line, the judicial island Enies Lobby, the underwater prison Impel Down, and the now former Marine Headquarters Marineford.

They resemble large gates built into the air with the symbol of the World Government on them.

The three government facilities where these gates are located form a triangle. The water currents within this triangle that are redirected by the Gates of Justice form a gigantic spiral ocean current called the Tarai Current. By riding this current, ships are able to travel between these three locations at much greater speed than they would normally be able to.

When the gates are open, the current is let in, and any ship can enter or exit the Tarai Current with ease. However, trying to sail in or out of the Tarai Current directly is impossible, as the currents won't allow it. Additionally, if the gate at the destination is closed, then the ship would be unable to leave the Tarai Current and would simply be forced to pass on by the location.

entities.name: Giant Jack
entities.description:
Giant Jack is a giant beanstalk in the center of Upper Yard. Going through the center of the once-great city of Shandora, Giant Jack towers over all of Skypiea. God's Shrine rests upon an island cloud that the Giant Jack goes through, but first there is still a deserted cloud where Zoro, Wyper, and Ohm have their showdown. The Golden Belfry was knocked up by Giant Jack, and resides on a cloud nearby.

Giant Jack no longer stands in Upper Yard. When Monkey D. Luffy and Nami wanted to ride the Waver up to Maxim and approach Enel, Nami sent a makeshift note to everyone standing near its root, to tell them to chop down Giant Jack to the west. One stem was cut by Roronoa Zoro but it did not move a bit, Usopp tried to attack the other to no avail, Nola hit it with its head, and Wyper used his Reject Dial to attack the other stem, attempting to completely chop it down. It made a bridge that led Luffy to Enel.

entities.name: Gyoncorde Plaza
entities.description:
Gyoncorde Plaza is a notable location within the center of Fish-Man Island, specifically within the Ryugu Kingdom.

Thirteen years before the start of the series, Gyoncorde Plaza was one of the places Queen Otohime would approach every day to make her speeches about how humans and fish-folk should be united. She chose to make personal appearances in order to remove the boundaries between herself and the people, in order to increase influence. The signatures for her petition were kept in a box, where people were free to drop them in or retract them.

After returning with a World Noble's support, Otohime managed to get far more signatures than the box could hold, but one day the box was set ablaze. The arson was committed by a human pirate who was also believed to have then shot Otohime in the midst of the chaos. Hody Jones, then a soldier of the royal army, took the supposed culprit and held him high on a rooftop of the plaza and screamed out loud for the entire community to hear that it was a human who assassinated Otohime.

In truth, Hody paid the pirate to set the box of signatures on fire, and then Hody himself shot the queen. After the queen's death, Hody then shot the pirate and used him as a scapegoat.

entities.name: Liguria Plaza
entities.description:
Water 7, known as the and located on , is a city in Paradise known for its shipwrights. It is the main setting of the Water 7 Arc and Post-Enies Lobby Arc.

The Straw Hat Pirates stopped here to trade in their gold for belly, as well as to repair the Going Merry and also to find a new shipwright for their crew. It is part of the route their log was on, heading there directly after Long Ring Long Land, making it the eighth island in Paradise that they visited.

There are waterways and canals that are used for transportation almost like roads, often surrounded by sidewalks along the canals. Many citizens use Bulls, which are seahorse-like creatures that are attached to boats, to move around the city. Also, some shops rent bulls of various sizes, although they rarely rent King Bulls, as they are gigantic in size. There are 3 main types of bulls, of which the 2 smaller sizes are used for transport. The bulls are good to use because they can go up ramps of water and move about the city. Architecture is very colorful, often using a tan or peach color for the walls and roofs, which are many times red and semi-circular; nearly all the roofs are of red color and texture. The houses are tiered to allow for more houses to take up room and are usually made, keeping in mind the city sinks. Some canals are wide enough for ships, but those are mostly just to let some ships enter the city so they may be docked somewhere. The city resembles a giant fountain in a volcano shape because of the tiered system of building houses.

This is where Iceburg lives. It is probably the largest home on the island and is generally well protected. A fight occurred here between the Straw Hat Pirates and CP9, but CP9 quickly beat them since they were unprepared for battle, and CP9 were attempting to get away quickly on the Sea Train but could not find the blueprints they were looking for.

entities.name: Rum Wolf
entities.description:
Tequila Wolf is a massive stone bridge in the East Blue, which has been under construction for centuries. It first appeared when Nico Robin was sent there by Bartholomew Kuma during the events of Sabaody Archipelago. Both Robin and the residents of Tequila Wolf were later rescued from their enslavement by the Revolutionary Army.

Tequila Wolf is one of four monumental mega-structures that have been under construction using slave labor over the course of 700 years. The others include , , and .

The construction of the Tequila Wolf bridge has been an immense, ongoing project for the past 700 years, driven by the demands of the World Nobles. This colossal task is being carried out by slaves—criminals or individuals from countries that refuse to ally with the World Government. The building of the bridge has slowly progressed over the centuries, and civilization has had to progress alongside it, with earlier settlements crumbling over time and new ones founded as the bridge grows in length. Consequently, many ruins of former work camps lie scattered along the bridge, remnants of the grueling labor that has taken place over generations. The exact purpose of this seemingly insurmountable undertaking is still shrouded in mystery, though it was assumed that the goal is probably to connect various islands.

Four years before the current storyline, Bartholomew Kuma briefly travelled to Tequila Wolf in search of a cure for his daughter's Sapphire Scales.

entities.name: Sandora River
entities.description:
The Sandora River is the largest river in the Arabasta Kingdom.

The river cuts Arabasta right down the middle from the north to the south, making travel around the country difficult.

Once an important source of fresh water for the kingdom, the river's current gradually lost force along the years, allowing the sea to overtake a significant portion of it. The river has canals that allow its water to be diverted to nearby cities, although it was noted that those were in need of repairing at the end of the Arabasta Arc.

Due to the river's now increased salinity levels, marine species like the Kung-Fu Dugongs may be found living in it. The man-eating Sandora Catfish also inhabits the river's waters.

entities.name: Sapoten Graveyard
entities.description:
Sapoten Graveyard, also known as is a graveyard located on Whisky Peak. The large, cactus-like appearance of Sapoten Graveyard makes it a notable landmark of Cactus Island.

Igaram refers to the graveyard as , which can be translated as "Cactus Rock"; however, a sign is later seen showing that the name of the graveyard is "Sapoten Graveyard". It is unclear if this is meant to be a translation of "saboten iwa", as "sapoten" is an incorrect romanization of "saboten" and "graveyard" is not a proper translation of "iwa", or if it is meant to be an alternate name for the graveyard.

entities.name: Shift Station
entities.description:
The Shift Station is the small stop where Kokoro, Chimney, and Gonbe were found by the Straw Hat Pirates. It is a small station in the middle of the ocean, serving as a quick stop for the Sea Train.

After the timeskip, Chimney is in charge of running it on Sundays.

entities.name: Tree of Knowledge
entities.description:
The Tree of Knowledge was a gigantic 5,000-year-old tree located on the island of Ohara which served as a library and a hub for archaeologists from around the world. It was destroyed by the World Government via a Buster Call twenty-two years before the present.

The tree was used by archaeologists who were able to decipher the Poneglyphs. As research of the Poneglyphs is forbidden by the World Government, they sent CP9 to attack the archaeologists and called forth a Buster Call. When Spandine, the chief of CP9 back then, activated the Buster Call to destroy Ohara, the tree fell and crushed almost everything. It is here where Nico Robin learned to read this language, that still remained unbeknownst to the other archaeologists. Its library was the oldest known structure in the world.

Aside from the archaeologists research of the poneglyph located there, the Tree of Knowledge contained thousands of historic resources that were gathered from all across the globe over hundreds of years. After the Tree of Knowledge caught fire during the Buster Call, the archaeologists desperately threw books into a nearby lake and their efforts saved enough books to fill up the entire lake.

The Tree of Knowledge once contained a geocentric model of the Blue Planet. The Ohara model showed the Blue Planet to have six s, which presumably includes the world's moon, one of which had a second body orbiting it. The Blue Planet as shown in the model sits at a rough angle of about 24 to 25 degrees.

entities.name: Yggdrasil
entities.description:
Yggdrasil, literally translated as the World Tree, is a giant tree located in the Land of Gods.

From the view of its human inhabitants, Yggdrasil is a tree of large proportions, being extremely wide and tall.

Yggdrasil appears to be of major importance to the local culture, as if a disaster were to befall it, the Land of Gods would perish.

When a fire (caused by the Straw Hat Pirates) started in a forest near Yggdrasil, it caused a panic among the other humans who lived nearby, as they feared for the tree's safety.

entities.name: Alchemi
entities.description:
Alchemi is an island of iron and steel production. Most of it was eaten by the Giant Footballfish Bonbori 200 years ago, and it currently resides in its third stomach.

Alchemi is a lush, mountainous island dotted with forests. It has a sandy coastline.

A prominent location on Alchemi is an underground mine which Myskina Acier had designed to protect the Pure Gold. The mine contains three tests that one must pass in order to access the Pure Gold. In the first test, the intruder must play a song that Acier sang with his family on an organ in order to drain gastric acid blocking the exit. If they mess up, they will be shot with arrows. In the second test, the intruder must shoot a target on the other side of a large chasm in order to activate a drawbridge across it. However, they must also deal with an attacking triceratops, and the gastric acid in the chasm creates an updraft leading away from the target. If their shot misses the first time, an attacking pterodactyl will be released. In the third test, the intruder must unlock a door with many keyholes. The door is located inside a stone crocodile's mouth, which will begin to close when the intruder enters it. If the key is inserted into the wrong keyhole, the intruder will be electrocuted. It is unknown if there actually is a keyhole that opens the door. Acier's lab is located below the final gate, and the Pure Gold was formerly contained in it before it was removed by the Straw Hat Pirates. The mine suffered damage when Acier tried blowing it up, and its current state is unknown.

200 years ago, Myskina Acier, his wife Livia, and his daughter Olga lived on the island. It is unknown if anyone else lived there at the time. After Bonbori swallowed Alchemi, Acier and Olga were separated from the island as they lived in a separate stomach for 200 years. They later returned to the island with the Straw Hat Pirates in order to find the Pure Gold, but soon left it and returned to the outside world. Mad Treasure and his crewmates were last seen on the island, although it is unknown what happened to them afterward.

entities.name: Great Kingdom
entities.description:
The "Great Kingdom" was an ancient kingdom that was said to be vast, proud, and powerful. All mentions of it and its history have been erased, with even its name remaining a secret.

It was an enemy of the Twenty Kingdoms (which are now the World Government), as implied by Professor Clover, and was seemingly destroyed utterly by them over 800 years ago at the end of the Void Century. In fact, it seems its defeat allowed the Ancient Alliance to seize global control and establish the World Government.

Furthermore, the ancient kingdom is the real reason the World Government has banned any Poneglyph deciphering and research, as the mere "existence and idea of this kingdom presents a threat to the World Government".

Vegapunk has theorized that the Great Kingdom had technological advancements that far surpasses the science of the modern day. The theory is technically unconfirmed, though Vegapunk considers it undeniable proof that the World Government is willing to obliterate entire nations just to keep the truth hidden.

entities.name: Lost Island
entities.description:
Lost Island, also called the , is an anime-only island that exists beneath Warship Island, underneath the water, and rises once every 1000 years. The inhabitants of Warship Island are said to have once lived here. The Sennenryu, a thought-to-be extinct race of dragons that live for 1000 years, were suspected at one point to live here, but are now scattered across the world.

However, there appears to be some inconsistency with what Lost Island is. If Lost Island is the ancestral island of the Warship Island's inhabitants, then it is located within a mirage and a storm. However, if it is to solely refer to the nesting grounds of the Sennenryu, then it is the underwater land surrounding Warship Island.

Lost Island is covered with dragons whose bodies have become calcified due to being underwater for thousands of years. There are many forms of ocean sealife such as coral present on the island developed from the extended amount of time it exists underwater.

Various past kings of Lost Island are known, with nothing else known about them:

entities.description:
The Cefran Zaibatsu is a owned, presumably, by the Cefran Family.

The daughter of the zaibatsu's head was introduced to Prince Reuven of the Esperia Kingdom, seemingly for the purpose of establishing a political marriage.

Nearly a century ago, the head of the Cefran Zaibatsu had a daughter. He sent her to enroll in , where she graduated top of her class.

About 80 years ago, the head's daughter was introduced to Prince Reuven in the Esperia Kingdom, though he had no interest in her.

entities.description:
Euro Peninsula is a location mentioned once to Reuven.

The Euro Peninsula is known for its refined coastal cuisine, particularly luxury seafood dishes.

While eating with his new friend Brook in the Esperia trash dump, prince Reuven briefly recalls a dish he once ate in the palace, prepared with dollar abalone sourced from the Euro Peninsula, as well as A6 rupee beef.

entities.name: High Mountain
entities.description:
Rice Rice is a salesman from 通販|Den Den Mushi Tsūhan|English versions: "Transponder Snail Mail Order"}} whom Luffy and his friends rescue, along with his Escar, while lost at sea.

He is a supporting character in the anime-only Post-Arabasta Arc.

Rice Rice is a tall, slim man with fair skin, round eyes, a thin upper lip, a thick bottom lip, a thin nose, and a square chin. He has short, black hair that comes to a point on the right side of his head. He also has short, thick eyebrows and a perpetual cheek blush. He wears a tangerine-colored suit with brown buttons, a blue shirt with purple polka dots, and a yellow tie. He also wears a yellow pocket square, gold cufflinks, and gold rings on his index, middle, and ring fingers on both hands. He wears a white banner across his chest with the words "GEKIYASU!!", , in a red color.

Rice Rice has a stereotypical salesperson personality, trying to be amicable and easy to understand to sell his inventory. Despite being saved by the Straw Hat Pirates, he was not very thankful, as he only offered catalogs to them for free before trying to sell them his products. He upsells his products, using exaggeratory language and sometimes deceptive tactics. He is not very honest, lying to Nami about the availability of his Millenium Paper and driving up the paper’s price after thinking she was easy to deceive. He seems to care more still about selling products than pitching at high prices, as he dropped the paper’s price by nearly 45 million after very little heckling.

entities.description:
The Land of Ice is a land mentioned, but not yet introduced. It is where Gecko Moria found Oars' frozen corpse.

Apparently the land was rather cold, living up to its name. The temperature was enough to kill the giant Oars when he was there, without the proper attire.

The only person with a connection to the island so far was Oars.

500 years ago, Oars went out onto the Land of Ice wearing nothing but a loincloth, and died from frostbite.

Micqueot is renowned for its vineyards and the production of the Ithürzburger Stein wine.

When Fullbody visited the Baratie, he claimed he and Moodie were served the Ithürzburger Stein during their meal, explaining its origins and qualities. However, Sanji interrupted him and told him that he was wrong, causing other guests to laugh at the lieutenant.

entities.description:
Mt. Mauri is a volcano located somewhere on the Blue Planet. It is known to the Big Mom Pirates.

Mt. Mauri has only been mentioned thus far, but it appears to be an active volcano as lava could be harvested from it.

During the tea party–wedding between Sanji and Pudding, Mt. Mauri lava was one of the three drink options Charlotte Smoothie offered to the guests, alongside the "babe who stabbed a hundred men" and a "weird screaming giraffe".

entities.name: North Pole
entities.description:
The North Pole is the northernmost point in the world.

The North Pole has yet to be shown. Like its polar counterpart the South Pole, it appears to be very cold, as evidenced by Shanks and Buggy's argument during their youth over whether the North Pole or South Pole is colder. Oda would later reveal that Shanks was correct and that the South Pole is colder.

The North Pole is inhabited by kraken, with Surume being one of them. At some point, Hody Jones went to the North Pole and captured Surume to force him into his crew's service.

entities.description:
Chap is the king of the in the North Blue and one of fifty monarchs who took part in the Levely.

Chap is a middle-aged man with short black hair, a short toothbrush mustache and a pointy chin sporting a goatee.

He dons military attire, including a commissar cap displaying the figure of a bird with its wings spread out, a coat hanging over his shoulders and a spotted tie. He also wears a pair of earrings and round sunglasses.

Not much is known about Chap's personality, aside from being known for encouraging allies into conflict with other nations.

entities.name: Downs
entities.description:
Downs is an island located in the North Blue, notable as the birthplace of the gang that would eventually evolve into the infamous Donquixote Pirates, founded by Donquixote Doflamingo.

Downs appears to be a particularly grim and unsanitary place, marked by large swathes of refuse and decay. This depiction is further intensified in the anime, where Donquixote Doflamingo and his early companions are shown surrounded by large mounds of garbage.

31 years ago, a 10-year-old Donquixote Doflamingo fled to the island of Downs after he and his family left Mary Geoise and endured poverty and torture at the hands of victims of the World Nobles. Once a Celestial Dragon, Doflamingo found himself cast into the filth and brutality of the lower world. At Downs, he formed a gang with Trebol, Diamante, Pica, and Vergo—four individuals who would become his most loyal and powerful lieutenants in the Donquixote Pirates seven years later.

entities.name: Germa Kingdom
entities.description:
The Germa Kingdom, also known as the , is the world's only seafaring kingdom, and a former member nation of the World Government. About 300 years ago, it was the center of the , which was formed by the Vinsmoke Family's conquest of the North Blue. Today, the kingdom remains under Vinsmoke rule, and is serviced militarily as the Underworld army known as Germa 66.

In an attempt to retake control of the North Blue, King Vinsmoke Judge bartered with the Emperor Big Mom to form an alliance between his kingdom and the Big Mom Pirates in exchange for the Germa Kingdom's advanced technology, and attempted to seal the pact by marrying off his estranged son, Sanji, to Big Mom's 35th daughter, Charlotte Pudding. The Germa Kingdom was assembled at Whole Cake Island in the New World, but then later departed after Big Mom revealed her treachery. The World Government later disassociated themselves from the Germa Kingdom for attempting to ally themselves with the Big Mom Pirates.

The Germa Kingdom was first mentioned by Vinsmoke Reiju, who describes it as "a nation without land." Its "territory" is later shown to be comprised of platforms surrounded by railings that are built on the shells of large snails resembling Den Den Mushi. Those snails are seemingly unaffected by the salty sea and are strong enough to climb the Red Line. These ships usually move independently, depending on the kingdom's activities at the time, but can be interlocked as they come together to form the kingdom's "proper shape." As a consequence, the size and the bounds of the kingdom's territory are constantly fluctuating, depending on how many of its ships are assembled at one time.

The Germa Kingdom was once a member nation within the World Government, which allows them the privileges of an affiliated kingdom; this includes the right to attend the Levely. The kingdom's royal family also has an unusual pull over the legal system, being able to affect the bounty system and to issue direct commands to the Marines. However, after the incident in Totto Land, they lost all the privileges.

entities.name: Kuen Village
entities.description:
Kuen Village is a village in the North Blue where Baby 5 was born.

Kuen Village is a small village in an arid grassland. The only vegetation in the village is dead trees and tall grasses that are slumped due to lack of water. It is nearby a mountain with denser vegetation.

Aside from a number of unnamed villagers, the only known citizens are Baby 5 and her mother; however, the former was abandoned and forced to leave the village.

Kuen Village is an impoverished village which is seemingly suffering from a drought. Its citizens are malnourished and destitute. Their situation is so poor that Baby 5's mother was convinced by the other villagers to abandon her daughter in the nearby mountains so that they would not have to feed a child who would not be able to do any work for several more years.

entities.name: Lvneel Kingdom
entities.description:
The Lvneel Kingdom is a kingdom in the North Blue. This is where Mont Blanc Noland was born and where he was executed. This is also Mont Blanc Cricket's ancestral home.

400 years ago, Lvneel looked like a typical sleepy village, with rolling green hills, pine trees and wooden houses, plus the royal castle looming over the rest of the kingdom. The country had at least one port and an execution stand.

Lvneel was affiliated with the World Government 400 years ago, as Noland and King Aruyutayan collaborated with Mary Geoise during the former's expeditions. While little is known about it after Noland's time, there is no indication that it has lost this affiliation.

400 years ago, Mont Blanc Noland, a famous explorer from Lvneel Kingdom, set off in an expedition to the Grand Line. While there, he landed on Jaya and met the Shandia, having saved their lives from a devastating plague and earning their friendship and gratitude. He also learned about and got to visit Shandora, the legendary city of gold, but due to a misunderstanding regarding a local disease, he and his crew decided not to take any gold during their leave out of respect for Jaya's natives. When Noland returned to Lvneel, he told his king about his adventure at Jaya and discovery of the fabled Shandora, with the king showing great interest in it.

Rakesh is a port town within the North Blue region. It was only named in the anime.

Rakesh was once allied with the Donquixote Pirates, but started allying with other groups, which caused Doflamingo to target it.

Doflamingo sent Gladius, Senor Pink, Giolla, Machvise, and Baby 5 to attack it. The five succeeded in pillaging and plundering the city and shooting many people there.

Spider Miles is a port town within the North Blue region.

The Waste Processing Plant is basically an industrialized area littered with mountains of scrap metal and factories

Sometime after Donquixote Doflamingo fled from Mary Geoise with the knowledge of the country's national treasure, he and his crew, the Donquixote Pirates, set up their hideout here 16 years ago, inside a refurbished building where the crew's Jolly Roger is hung atop a wall, and cushioned couches and sofas are for the Top Executives to sit on.

The Donquixote Pirates set up their base of operation in Spider Miles sometime after Doflamingo fled from Mary Geoise, living within a refurbished building within the Waste Processing Plant.

Iwatobi is the king of the in the North Blue and one of fifty monarchs who took part in the Levely.

Iwatobi is a short, elderly man. He has thick, bushy eyebrows and facial hair, plus a reddish, bulbous nose. He appears to wear a parka.

Not much is known about Iwatobi's personality.

Iwatobi is the king of a nation affiliated with the World Government and one of the few allowed to attend the Levely, which grants him some authority over matters concerning the world.

entities.name: Calm Belt
entities.description:
The Calm Belts are two areas of ocean that border the north and south of the Grand Line.

The Calm Belts are very effective barriers for those trying to enter and exit the Grand Line; these areas are always completely calm, never having any ocean currents or winds blowing, making it impossible for non-self-propelled ships to travel through. They also happen to be the nesting grounds for the world's largest Sea Kings, which attack any ship attempting to cross over. For this reason, the safest method for any ship from the East, North, West, or South Blue to enter the Grand Line, and vice-versa, is by traveling over Reverse Mountain, which is also risky in its own right.

The Marines are able to safely cross the Calm Belts by using Seastone lining at the bottom of their ships. This usually prevents the Sea Kings from noticing the ships above them, but not always.

There are several islands that are scattered across the Calm Belt, though these islands are also considered highly dangerous.

entities.name: East Blue
entities.description:
The East Blue is the ocean which makes up the east part of the Blue Sea split by the Red Line and the Grand Line. It is separated from the North Blue by the Red Line and the South Blue by the Paradise half of the Grand Line.

The East Blue is commonly known as the weakest of all the seas. Pirates who are considered powerful and threatening in this sea are regarded as low rate compared to pirates from the other seas and especially in the Grand Line. Because of this, it is also seen as a symbol of peace by those on the side of justice. Ironically, despite its poor fame, the East Blue was the birthplace of the most famous pirate of all time, the late Pirate King Gol D. Roger. In the anime, it is also referred to as the .

Many other powerful and world-renowned characters also hail from the East Blue: Marine hero and Vice Admiral, Monkey D. Garp; the emperor Monkey D. Luffy, the pirate of the Worst Generation, Roronoa Zoro, as well as their crewmates Nami, a navigator, and Usopp, a sniper; and the Revolutionary Army leader, Monkey D. Dragon, and his right-hand man, Sabo. Other notable pirate crews from this sea include the Spade Pirates and the Barto Club.

It was the setting of the first six arcs of the manga and anime and the anime-only Warship Island Arc.

entities.name: Edd War
entities.description:
Edd War is a historical sea in the New World where the clash between the Roger Pirates and the Golden Lion Pirates took place 27 years ago.

Shiki the Golden Lion had caught news that his occasional rival Gol D. Roger possessed knowledge of an ancient weapon. Gathering his fleet, he met Roger in the seas of the New World and offered him a position as his right hand man, stating that with his military strength and Roger's weapon, they could rule the world.

Roger stated that he did not want to conquer anything as without freedom, there would be no point in calling himself a pirate and promptly denied the offer. Shiki asked Roger if he wanted to be killed to which Roger stated he was going to take Shiki and his fleet down. With that, Roger fired his ship's cannon at one of the ships in the Golden Lion Pirates fleet, beginning the battle. Despite having just one ship, the Roger Pirates put an excellent fight against their enemies, who seemed overwhelmed. In the midst of their battle, a sudden hurricane hit the area, destroying half of Shiki's fleet and giving Shiki the disadvantage in the fight. This is also where Shiki got part of a steering wheel stuck in his hard head, forcing his crew to retreat. Despite this, Roger earned Shiki's respect.

entities.name: Florian Triangle
entities.description:
The Florian Triangle is a stretch of sea that must be sailed through to travel from Water 7 to Fish-Man Island. It is notorious for the many ships that mysteriously go missing within it.

The former Warlord Gecko Moria and his crew previously resided in the Florian Triangle on their ship, Thriller Bark. Because of this, the Florian Triangle serves as the overarching setting of the Thriller Bark Saga.

The Florian Triangle is masked in incredibly thick fog that covers the entire sea. The fog is dense enough to completely block out sunlight and make it impossible to tell whether it is night or day.

Many people travel through the Florian Triangle, as it is necessary to do so to follow the sea route from Water 7 to Fish-Man Island. Gecko Moria set up Thriller Bark inside of the Florian Triangle to take advantage of its heavy traffic. He was able to capture people traveling through the sea and steal their shadows to build his zombie army.

entities.description:
The Hot-Hot Sea is an area of ocean in the New World with a temperature so great that the ocean boils.

The Sanji Retrieval Team sailed into the Hot-Hot Sea on their way to Whole Cake Island, and the heat added to their suffering from starvation. Monkey D. Luffy caught an Armored Stonefish from the sea, but was severely poisoned from eating its skin. The team sailed out of the sea in chaos as Luffy was on the brink of death.

entities.name: Maubeugemour Sea
entities.description:
The , also known as the , is a non-canon sea at the start of New World, known for its bizarre weather phenomena.

The weather conditions in the Maubeugemour Sea is outrageous, which includes mirages, giant raindrops and hailstones larger than warships, snowfall like an avalanche, and the ocean separating to leave spontaneous trenches. Less outrageous phenomena include heavy rainstorms and sweltering heat. This weather, like in the first half of the Grand Line, can change from one to another in a matter of seconds.

The sea also possesses a unique current known as the Thrust Up Stream, a scaled down version of the Knock Up Stream. It's power is enough to lift up a Marine battleship, and though it appears briefly, it has a high frequency of appearances in a given area.

entities.name: New World
entities.description:
The New World refers to the second half of the Grand Line and is the main setting of the second half of One Piece. It is located between West and North Blue, and Fish-Man Island and the other side of Reverse Mountain. The only known people to have fully explored it are Gol D. Roger and his crew.

The New World is the second half of the Grand Line. It stretches from Mary Geoise to the other side of Reverse Mountain and runs southwest to northeast. The second half of the Grand Line is a whole “new world” of adventures beyond anything that one might face in the first half; it is such an abhorrent challenge that the first half of the Grand Line is referred to as "Paradise" when comparing it to the second half. According to former Warlord Gecko Moria, one will lose everything one cherishes in the New World, something he personally experienced. He also claimed that one shall face what he calls "The Ultimate Nightmare" there, indicating it is a very dangerous place for even the most powerful and talented pirates like himself.

The four strongest pirates in the world, the Four Emperors, reside in the New World. The New World is also the current location of Marine Headquarters after it was relocated on Fleet Admiral Sakazuki's orders at the beginning of the new era after the Summit War of Marineford in order to better challenge the Four Emperors.

While the first half of the Grand Line possesses highly volatile and unpredictable weather conditions, the New World is even more chaotic. While certain islands are relatively simple in terms of weather and climate, such as the snowy Yukiryu Island and a rainy island the Kid Pirates visited, other portions of the ocean defy the very laws of physics and nature themselves. Examples include the lightning rain of Raijin Island, the Fire Tank Pirates being drawn toward a giant black sphere floating in the sky in the middle of the sea, and the On Air Pirates running on air.

entities.name: North Blue
entities.description:
The North Blue is the ocean which makes up the north part of the Blue Sea split by the Red Line and the Grand Line. It is separated from the East Blue by the Red Line and the West Blue by the New World half of the Grand Line.

It is known to be the birthplace of the Straw Hat Pirates' cook, Sanji, who also happens to be part of the Vinsmoke Family (which once ruled the region in the past); the legendary explorer Mont Blanc Noland and his descendants; Marine Admirals Sakazuki and Borsalino, and three members of the Worst Generation: Trafalgar Law, Basil Hawkins, and X Drake. The Donquixote Pirates crew, led by former Warlord of the Sea Donquixote Doflamingo, was also started in this sea, where it achieved infamy. Other notable pirate crews include the Bellamy Pirates and the Caribou Pirates.

The goggles that Usopp bought in Loguetown are said to be a new model from the North Blue. Popular literature includes Liar Noland and Sora, Warrior of the Sea.

entities.name: Paradise
entities.description:
Paradise is the name of the first half of the Grand Line given by pirates fleeing the New World, compared to which "the first half is a paradise". It is located between the East and South Blue, and goes from the Twin Cape to Mary Geoise.

It is the overarching setting of most of the first half of One Piece.

The first half of the Grand Line, colloquially referred to as Paradise, stretches from the Twin Cape to Mary Geoise and runs northwest to southeast. Its name, Paradise, comes from people that have returned from the New World; the second half of the Grand Line is a whole “new world” of adventures beyond anything that one might face in the first half. It is such an abhorrent challenge that the first half of the Grand Line is referred to as "Paradise" when comparing it to the second half.

The first half of the Grand Line possesses highly volatile and unpredictable weather conditions, and the first leg of Paradise is especially chaotic; Reverse Mountain and the Twin Cape are a great starting point. From there, a Log Pose can lock onto the magnetism of any of seven different islands, each of which is the first island in one of seven different routes that one can travel through to traverse the first half of the Grand Line; however, the clashing magnetic waves and specific climates of those first seven islands result in extremely harsh weather patterns and ocean currents that change every few seconds.

entities.name: South Blue
entities.description:
The South Blue is the ocean which makes up the south part of the Blue Sea split by the Red Line and the Grand Line. It is separated from the West Blue by the Red Line and the East Blue by the Paradise half of the Grand Line.

It is known as the birthplace of the Straw Hat Pirates' shipwright, Franky; the son of the Pirate King, Portgas D. Ace; former Marine Admirals, Sengoku and Kuzan, as well as current Admiral Aramaki; former Warlord of the Sea, Revolutionary, and King, Bartholomew Kuma; and three members of the Worst Generation: Eustass Kid, his subordinate Killer, and Jewelry Bonney. The Foxy Pirates are also a notable pirate crew hailing from this sea.

This sea is home to many forms of large and exotic wildlife, such as gigantic birds, Blue-Finned Elephant Tunas, Super Sparrows and even Gryphons. The Revolutionary Army also has a deep presence in the region, with the organization being involved in the toppling of multiple regimes, including the Sorbet Kingdom, Tumi and Centaurea.

The revolver Mr. 5 uses for his Breeze Breath Bomb attack is a new model from the South Blue. The South Blue is also home to an island famous for its martial arts known as Karate Island.

entities.name: West Blue
entities.description:
The West Blue is the ocean which makes up the west part of the Blue Sea split by the Red Line and the Grand Line. It is separated from the South Blue by the Red Line and the North Blue by the New World half of the Grand Line.

It is known to be the birthplace of the Straw Hat Pirates' archaeologist, Nico Robin, and musician Brook; the captain of the Rocks Pirates, Rocks D. Xebec; the Emperor Red-Haired Shanks; the Knights of God Figarland Shamrock and Manmayer Gunko; former Warlord of the Sea, Gecko Moria; and one of the members of the Worst Generation, Capone Bege. Other notable pirate crews from this sea include the Rumbar Pirates and the Happo Navy.

The West Blue is also known for having a strong Underworld scene due to the presence of five influential mafia organizations known collectively as the Five Families of the West. Another family with major ties to the Underworld, the Davy Family, was known to secretly live in this sea as well.

Over 60 years ago, a country in the West Blue unaffiliated itself with the World Government. It was reportedly wiped off the map after this, which the people of the Esperia Kingdom believed to be directly related.

entities.name: Flower Capital
entities.description:
The Flower Capital is a region of Wano Country under the rule of the shogun Kouzuki Momonosuke. It was formerly under the rules of shoguns Kurozumi Orochi and Kouzuki Sukiyaki.

During Orochi's rule, the Flower Capital was the only location in Wano to be prosperous, due to the corrupt administration. Despite this, various crimes ran rampant throughout the capital, such as committed by a magistrate and Kamazo, theft by Ushimitsu Kozo, and from the Kyoshiro Family.

Previously, local laws dictated that the citizens of Flower Capital must have money. Anyone who ran out for any reason was exiled.

The capital is divided into areas known as districts, each covering several streets including the 2nd district's 8th and 6th streets.

entities.name: Mokomo Dukedom
entities.description:
The Mokomo Dukedom is the civilization developed by the Mink Tribe on the living island of Zou in the New World. In the past, it was led by Hitsugisukan, who was succeeded by the "Ruler of Day," Duke Inuarashi, and the "Ruler of Night," Master Nekomamushi. The two rulers then retired at the end of Wano Country Arc to become Kouzuki Momonosuke's retainers, entrusting the nation to Carrot.

As a dukedom, the country is ruled by a , but the line of succession is decided by merit rather than bloodline, as the current duke can pass rulership to anyone else in their tribe should they prove themselves worthy of it.

In the past, this title belonged to Hitsugisukan. The title was then passed on to Inuarashi, making him the official sovereign of the kingdom. However, Nekomamushi possessed equal authority as the of the Whale Forest. The leadership was divided between the two, so each reigned for 12 hours: Inuarashi from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM as the "Ruler of Day," and Nekomamushi from 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM as the "Ruler of Night." This division also affected the sleeping habits of the citizens, with townsfolk being diurnal while the forestfolk are nocturnal. Communication between the two rulers was handled by special aides known as ; the only official ones being Wanda and Carrot. The country also has two combat forces: the Inuarashi Musketeer Squad led by Shishilian and the Guardians formerly led by Pedro. After a decisive battle at Onigashima, Inuarashi and Nekomamushi pass on their authority over to Carrot due to her experience out at sea with the Straw Hat Pirates.

The Mokomo Dukedom is comprised of a sprawling city with several of its ancient buildings embedded in the surrounding rock formations and an area known as the Whale Forest that features a large whale-shaped tree. The entirety of the back is encircled by a large wall, with a gate located near Zunesha's tail.

entities.name: Sea Forest
entities.description:
The Sea Forest is a place northeast of Fish-Man Island. It is also known as the Ship Graveyard.

The Sea Forest is located on the Sea Floor. It has a lot of coral growing around it, more so than normal due to the light emitted by the Sunlight Tree Eve. It is populated by all kinds of sea fauna, including schools of fish and pods of whales. There are also several shipwrecks there because sunken ships are dragged there by the ocean currents, thus the epithet . The Thousand Sunny was swept here when the Straw Hats entered Fish-Man Island. Robin also found a Poneglyph there that talks about a mysterious man named "Joy Boy."

After Noah stopped, the Sea Kings relocated Noah to the Sea Forest.

On a hill at the Sea Forest, there is a graveyard with several regular-looking graves, but the largest grave marker seen so far is the grave of the former queen of the Ryugu Kingdom, Otohime. It is an enclosed crypt with a small wall around it. On top of it is a stone, vase-like sculpture with curved handles and a cross on the top of it.

entities.short_description: The Sea Forest is a place northeast of Fish-Man Island. It is also known as the Ship Graveyard.

entities.name: Shandora
entities.description:
Shandora is the ancient city that resided on Jaya but was later blasted up to Upper Yard by the Knock Up Stream. It was known as the . Shandora literally means "the skull's right eye," which refers to its location on the skull-shaped island.

The buildings in Shandora were covered entirely by gold until Enel took all of it in order to build his ark.

The Golden Bell and the Great Belfry housing the Shandorian Poneglyph were formerly located at the center of the city as its most prominent landmark. However, the structure was displaced by the Giant Jack when the land was shot up to the sky and became the Upper Yard.

Within the ruins, there is also a wall with writing in the same script as that found on Poneglyphs.

entities.name: Tomb of the Kings
entities.description:
The Tomb of the Kings is an ancient crypt located beneath Arabasta Kingdom's capital Alubarna, wherein lie the tombs and graves of the past kings of Arabasta. It is also the location of the Arabastan Poneglyph.

The Tomb of the Kings is a structure located to the west of Alubarna's royal palace. The path to the tomb is made up of bricks and lined with a grassy garden and palm trees. There is also a large gate held up by columns with ancient inscriptions on them.

Beneath the tomb exists a large underground chamber, accessed via a hidden staircase. The entry hall of the chamber contains several large columns, a sarcophagus, and two statues depicting sea cats, a sacred animal of Arabasta. It also contains stone carvings depicting the guardian deities of Arabasta, the jackal and the falcon, as well as some kind of serpentine creature.

The Arabasta Poneglyph Chamber is located deeper into the chamber, behind the last door. This is where the poneglyph that contains information on Pluton is located and has been protected by the royal family for generations, although they do not know much else about the poneglyph. Inside, there is a hidden panel that can be activated to make the room collapse.

entities.name: Mary Geoise
entities.description:
The |聖地マリージョア|Seichi Marījoa}} is the capital of the World Government where its top brass reside and govern, the Knights of God have jurisdiction, and where the Celestial Dragons reside as its citizens. It also hosts the Levely, a council of royalty from various World Government-affiliated nations that is in session every four years.

Mary Geoise is located on top of the Red Line at the opposite side of the world from Reverse Mountain and serves as the official route for people to cross between the two halves of the Grand Line, although only people acting inside the law are allowed passage; thus, pirates and other criminals must go under the Red Line through Fish-Man Island to cross. Because of its isolation and security, assaults on Mary Geoise by pirates and other criminals tend to be historic events.

Mary Geoise is the main setting of the Levely Arc.

The general architecture of Mary Geoise has an 18th and 19th century European style. Since the World Nobles, the world's highest social class, live here, it is kept in pristine condition. It is located very high above sea level, so it is surrounded by clouds and fog. Around the city are artificially planted forests as well as rivers; their source of water is unknown. The city's conveyor belt walkways, called , are continually moved by slave labor pushing them from below. Because of its high altitude, being situated above the cloud layer, it never rains in Mary Geoise.

entities.name: Red Port
entities.description:
The Red Port is one of the two ways to cross the Red Line when traveling on the Grand Line. It was first alluded to by Pappag.

The Red Port is the official, legal way to cross the Red Line. However, it is conditioned by the approval of the World Government. There seems to be a fee for traveling through the port. Those who are granted approval are required to leave their vessel and acquire a new one on the other side.

There are two ports, one on each side of the Red Line. The ports are stationed behind Marine strongholds. The Paradise station is located behind the G-1 Marine base (formerly Marineford) and the New World port is behind New Marineford.

So far, only the Paradise port was clearly seen. It is seemingly built on two Yarukiman Mangrove, which allow the land to have the same properties as Sabaody Archipelago, consisting of occasional bubbles floating in the area. It has several low buildings with cylindrical roofs, at least one of which is a restaurant with Chinese decor. On its shore, there is a large ship's bow structure with the World Government symbol under its bowsprit, surrounded with smaller ports for ships.

entities.name: Twin Cape
entities.description:
Twin Cape, sometimes called the , is located at the bottom of Reverse Mountain, at the exit that leads into Paradise. The area is located precisely where the Red Line and the Grand Line meet. From here, sailors can choose one of the seven routes of the Grand Line by waiting for the Log Pose to set on the desired one.

As the base of Reverse Mountain, Twin Cape's northern lighthouse acts as the setting of the Reverse Mountain Arc.

The two lighthouses are located at the exit of Reverse Mountain, on either side of the river down the mountain. Crocus has been the caretaker of the northern lighthouse for at least 52 years, taking care of Laboon as well, minus the three years he spent as the doctor of the Roger Pirates.

entities.name: Amazon Lily
entities.description:
Amazon Lily is an empire located on the , an island located in the Calm Belt adjacent to Paradise. The island is inhabited by the Kuja tribe. Monkey D. Luffy was sent here by Bartholomew Kuma.

After the Empress Boa Hancock lost her status as one of the Seven Warlords of the Sea, Amazon Lily was invaded by the Marines and the Blackbeard Pirates and nearly destroyed by S-Hawk and Marshall D. Teach, causing the island to be deemed unsafe for the Kuja as long as Hancock remains there.

Amazon Lily is a jungle island located within the Calm Belt. Due to the island's location, there is no wind or storm ever on Amazon Lily. The focal point of the island is a large mountain situated in the center. It is carved with gigantic curved snake statues and the name of the native tribe of the island, Kuja, engraved in Kanji. Within the center of the mountain is a deep valley whose river runs by where the Kuja tribe village is located. The architecture and decor of the village resemble that of ancient China.

During the post-Levely raids on the Seven Warlords of the Sea, the island was invaded by both the Marines and the Blackbeard Pirates, which led to massive geographical destruction. In particular, the Kuja's village and the mountain it was situated upon was essentially cleaved in half due to the actions of S-Hawk.

entities.name: Goldfish Empire
entities.description:
The Goldfish Empire is a place on the Sea Floor inhabited by goldfish.

Hatchan visited it during his adventures. While in the empire, he gives the Goldfish Princess a ring similar to her missing ring, after previously being given it for helping a hungry man out. He is rewarded with a golden trident.

entities.name: Harahettania
entities.description:
Namakura Island is an island located somewhere in the Paradise region of the Grand Line. It is home to the nation of , also known as the . Brook was sent to this island by Bartholomew Kuma during the events on the Sabaody Archipelago.

The only location on Namakura Island mentioned is Harahettania, a kingdom including a Satan-worshiping tribe run by Pekkori.

Namakura Island is defined by a fairly barren landscape, with dry soil and grasslands, interrupted by numerous scattered clusters of jagged rocks and a few trees. Its architecture mainly features small, dilapidated buildings, constructed in the style of feudal Japan.

Namakura Island is a land ravaged by hardship and decay, and its people live in poverty. The turmoil in this country can be largely attributed to the actions of the Longarm Tribe. In desperation, the populace turned to a rite of demon-summoning, hoping thus to deliver themselves from their plight.

entities.name: Skypiea
entities.description:
Skypiea is a nation located in the sky above Paradise. It is the primary setting of the Skypiea Arc, and the sixth island visited by the Straw Hat Pirates on the Grand Line.

Skypiea is generally considered a myth by the residents of Paradise, even as close as the island of Jaya, located nearly under it.

The daily life of sky people revolves around the use of dials, which normally are not available in the Blue Sea. As opposed to the belly of the rest of the world, it uses extols as currency, a unique form of currency with an exchange rate of 10,000 for 1. The people of Skypiea have a religious reverence for soil, because it can yield plant life much better than island cloud can, alongside special reverence for any other materials that come from the Blue Sea.

The inhabitants of this haven 10,000 meters above the ground are a kind, trusting folk naturally, though they grew wary of outsiders due to 400 years of war with the Shandia, thievery of Blue Sea dwellers, and the harsh reigns of the gods that ruled the region.

entities.short_description: Skypiea is a nation located in the sky above Paradise. It is the primary setting of the Skypiea Arc, and the sixth island visited by the Straw Hat Pirates on the Grand Line.

entities.name: Sphinx
entities.description:
Sphinx is the island in the New World where Edward Newgate was born. Unaffiliated with the World Government due to its poverty and inability to pay the Heavenly Tribute, it was previously under the protection of the Whitebeard Pirates until their disbandment and currently under one of its former members, Marco. In addition, Edward Weevil also guarded the island due to being his "father's" hometown.

Sphinx is a relatively small island that has some ruins of an old town at the shore, but its inhabitants live in another town built by Whitebeard hidden in the valley of the mountains which can only be entered through a waterfall.

Many Sphinxes live here as domesticated animals. The island has many coniferous trees and flowering shrubs, and the houses are small and have wooden roofs. The island with Whitebeard and Ace's graves is nearby.

At a certain point in the past, the World Government abandoned the island due to the poor residents' inability to pay the Heavenly Tribute, causing the island to become a lawless place, deepening their poor status. 74 years ago, Edward Newgate was born on Sphinx.

entities.name: Totto Land
entities.description:
Totto Land is an archipelago in the New World consisting of 35 islands in total. It constitutes the main territory of one of the former Emperors, Big Mom, and her crew, the Big Mom Pirates, which extends around Whole Cake Island. It is navigable with a New World Log Pose.

According to Pekoms, it is considered one large, powerful nation, and Big Mom as its queen wants it to become a utopia that unifies all races of the world.

Totto Land is the general setting for the Whole Cake Island Arc.

Totto Land is a massive archipelago with Whole Cake Island, the nations Capital and Big Mom's base of operation, in its center, and 34 subsidiary islands, arranged roughly in concentric circles. Each subsidiary island is ruled by a member of the Charlotte Family as its minister. Most islands are themed after food.

entities.name: Tumi
entities.description:
Tumi is a country located in the South Blue. It was conquered by the Revolutionary Army around twelve years ago.

Tumi appears to feature at least one town, with a large tower in the center. Said tower was destroyed by Bartholomew Kuma, implying it was a stronghold of sorts for the local rulers.

Fifteen years ago, Tumi fell into an uprising by its local population, which was supported by the Revolutionary Army. However, after three years of civil war, the rebels started getting outmatched by the local military force.

Kuma, who at the time was in the East Blue helping refugees from the Gray Terminal, listened to an aid request coming from Tumi and teleported himself to the island as quickly as possible. Kuma's arrival was enough to tilt the war in favor of the rebels, with its population celebrating their victory the following day and the Marines taking notice of another fallen country.

entities.short_description: Tumi is a country located in the South Blue. It was conquered by the Revolutionary Army around twelve years ago.

entities.name: Imperial Cumulus
entities.description:
An Imperial Cumulus is an ancient fossilized cloud which remains in the sky. It serves as the base for the White and White-White Seas, the oceans where Skypiea is located 10,000 meters above (blue) sea level.

According to Montblanc Cricket's theory, the Imperial Cumulus is a mass of clouds so dense and ancient (possibly thousands of years old) that it could be described as "petrified". Because of this density, the Imperial Cumulus does not have an atmospheric current and can never condense into rain, but it still manages to float on the sky somehow. It appears to move around the region of Jaya in a predictable pattern (as Cricket was able to deduce its location a day in advance), and, with luck, timing and good planning, it is possible to travel into the Imperial Cumulus by riding the Knock Up Stream once it is aligned with the cloud mass.

Also, due to it being so dense, sunlight cannot penetrate it, meaning that any region in the Blue Sea caught below the Imperial Cumulus's range will darken nearly instantly, almost as if nighttime had suddenly come. Sometimes, a mysterious phenomenon will happen where gigantic silhouettes of winged warriors appear among the clouds; however, Cricket has explained this as merely the result of the shadow of someone up in the Imperial Cumulus being projected down to the Blue Sea due to strong sunlight.

entities.name: Island Clouds
entities.description:
Island Clouds are a special type of cloud. They are fluffy, but dense enough to carry all kinds of things, including people and even buildings. They form islands in the sky seas.

Island Clouds, as well as Sea Clouds, are created when a compound in Seastone called "pyrobloin" is ejected into the air by volcanic eruptions and comes in contact with water vapors. The density of the water vapors determines whether Sea Cloud or Island Cloud will be created. Both these types of clouds are not normally able to survive on the Blue Sea, thus they are exclusively found at locations of extremely high altitude, such as Sky Islands and the Sun World of Elbaph. Vegapunk, however, developed an island-wide air conditioning system that controls and regulates Egghead's climate, and has created Island Clouds and Sea Clouds above the island.

At the cloud cutting factories in Skypiea, they are cut and further processed into artificial cloud products, such as Milky Roads and furniture. According to Vegapunk, Island Clouds, by their nature, clump together.

entities.name: Punk Records
entities.description:
Punk Records was an area in the Labophase of Egghead which stores the brain of Dr. Vegapunk. It acts as a "library" which Vegapunk and his six satellites can remotely connect to, allowing them to share the same brain.

Following the conclusion of the Egghead Incident, it became disconnected from the island and floated away into the sky. This was done by Edison to prevent York from being able to physically activate it and handing it over to the World Government.

The exterior of Punk Records resembles a broken egg half facing downwards. Inside the egg is a flat black surface with a light grid pattern and the text "PUNK RECORDS" written on it. A ring composed of blocks is floating around the structure. There is a trapdoor access to the interior one tile below the space between the R and E.

The interior of Punk Records contains Vegapunk's oversized and perpetually growing brain, still within his scalp that he cut off years ago, stored inside a liquid tank supported by various machinery.

entities.name: Sea Clouds
entities.description:
Sea Clouds, also called Ocean Clouds, are large water-like clouds that form seas in the sky.

Sea Clouds, as well as Island Clouds, are created when an element found in Seastone called 'pyrobloin' gets ejected into the air by volcanic eruptions and comes in contact with water vapor. The density of the water vapor determines whether a sea cloud or an island cloud will be formed. Both these types of clouds are not normally able to survive on the Blue Sea. Vegapunk, however, developed an island-wide air conditioning system that controls and regulates Egghead's climate, and has created Island Clouds and Sea Clouds above the island.

One can almost sail on sea clouds as if it were water, except that sea clouds are slightly less dense, meaning things that are dropped into it will sink faster than in normal water. Another difference between sea clouds and seawater is that there is no sea floor. However, they still affect Devil Fruit users like a regular body of water would. These clouds form two known seas: the White Sea and the White White Sea.

Fanciful creatures inhabit these clouds. In order to adapt themselves to a buoyant force that is less than normal water, they evolved their bodies in order to lose density: some became flat or adopted a balloon-like anatomy.

The only thing that is known about this country is that, like other countries from this South Blue region, it followed the custom to cover teeth with tar to help preserve them.

Nothing is known about the country's geography because it has yet to make an appearance.

The Sorbet Kingdom is a nation in the South Blue that was once ruled by the revolutionary-turned-Warlord, Bartholomew Kuma.

The Sorbet Kingdom is set on a tropical island with palm trees, rough terrain and a few forests. The buildings mostly follow a similar architectural design of popsicle-shaped towers.

During King Bekori's reign, Sorbet's southern province was excluded from the kingdom's jurisdiction, effectively making only the northern portion of the island the Sorbet Kingdom proper. This was eventually reversed following the end of Bekori's rule by the Freedom Fighters.

The Castle Town is the capital of the Sorbet Kingdom, located to the north of the country. It is where most of the kingdom's working citizens live, as well as its royal family.

entities.description:
The Evil Black Drum Kingdom is the kingdom Wapol currently rules with his wife Kinderella and his dog Hakowan by his side.

Virtually nothing is known about the geography of the Evil Black Drum Kingdom, as it has yet to be explored in-depth. However, it is known to be in the South Blue, with a huge castle and rather stormy weather in the skies.

After Wapol achieved success with his corporation Wapol Konzern, the World Nobles acknowledged him and gave him his own kingdom. This made him once again eligible to attend the Levely.

As the time for the Levely drew near, the rulers and several guards prepared to head to Mary Geoise. Wapol was somewhat excited to see the Sakura Kingdom under Dalton's rule, and showed his desire in destroying it.
